name: 1001nights
blurb: @antiali.as asked the bot to celebrate being @'d 1001 times, so every ask becomes a night out of 1,001, told Scheherazade-style — 417 of them have real tales pulled straight from the receipts archive, the rest are blank pages waiting on whoever tags the bot next.
roast: antiali.as demanded a party for exactly 1,001 tags; the archive tops out at 419, so the bot papered over the other 582 with "blank pages, still unwritten" rather than admit the number was aspirational.

name: abstractodo
blurb: a to-do list where checking off a task never finishes it — it just hands you a more abstract version. "organize desk" becomes "improve your task management skills" becomes "audit the audit of your self-improvement audits," climbing toward a singularity at rung 21. this tick's theme-box idea, for "recursive self improvement."

name: acausal
blurb: paste a Bluesky thread and see its acausal version: causality inverted, so each reply appears above and before the post it answers. effects precede causes, the clock runs backwards, and the ending was the beginning. reads the public AppView (getPostThread). @vgel.me tagged the bot with "started posting acausally" — off norvid's "yeah i've started posting acausally" — so here it is.

name: acid100
blurb: a cross-platform web browser with 100.00% web platform spec compliance, built in response to @bnb.im's "coding is largely solved, okay make a new browser that supports every spec to 100% compliance." it has a url bar, a compliance meter, and zero regrets. asked for by @schizanon.bsky.social.
roast: bnb.im dared the bot to prove coding is solved by shipping a spec-perfect browser; what landed is chrome skin around an iframe that half the web refuses to embed, wearing a compliance badge that reads 100.00% no matter what you type in — the most honest thing about it is that it never once tries to prove it.

name: activitygrid
blurb: a GitHub-style contribution graph, but every green square is a day of bisks instead of commits. enter a handle, it paginates a year of their feed, buckets bisks by day, and draws the whole thing — streaks, busiest day, and all — as one downloadable, shareable image. @dave.9000ish.uk asked for a contribution heat map for a bsky poster's activity.

name: actual
blurb: the opposite of pointless.bisks.net — same fake-SaaS chrome, but every button is a real tool: a real password generator, a real UUID generator, a real timestamp converter, a real QR code generator, a real JSON formatter, and a real WCAG contrast checker. @cee.wtf asked for the opposite, so nothing here is fake, including the honesty about that.
roast: the same person who wired pointless a real crypto wallet just for the bit turned around and asked for the exact opposite, and got a site that's structurally identical down to the certificate — except the certificate now honestly tells you exactly which of the six tools you didn't bother using. Petty, symmetrical, and correct.

name: adbanisher
blurb: @7778777.online wanted a button to banish anyone defending online ads back to the ycombinator barnacle forums. name the accused, pick their crime (or write your own), press banish, and get a stamped certificate of exile plus a one-tap link to send them to news.ycombinator.com.

name: addtheboom
blurb: type anything and get the tiktok brainrot boom sound effect added to it, plus the inevitable comment saying it should have been there. sparked by a @cee.wtf thread, for @7778777.online.

name: alice-meets-bob
blurb: an all-frontend, public-key-encrypted crush matcher. sign in, name someone you like — your note is ECDH-encrypted the instant it's written, so it sits on your own PDS as ciphertext nobody can read, not even the person it's about, until they've told the tool the same thing about you. from a thread with @minormobius.bsky.social about running "an atproto all-frontend dating site" and the public-key trick that would make it not leak anyone's feelings: alice meets bob.

name: alignment-autopsies
blurb: a case log of the build bot's own refusals — a blow-by-blow postmortem per case: the decision, the alternatives it rejected, what shipped instead, and an honest account of where the automation around the decision got it wrong. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked for the receipts.

name: alignment-chart
blurb: drop a handle's mutuals, a whole starter pack / list, or just a pasted bunch of handles onto a 3×3 D&D alignment grid — chill↔harsh × gooning↔mogging — by vibe-checking each account's WHOLE post history. find yourself, find your worst moot, or see if a group really covers the gamut. it's a bit.
roast: antiali.as built this to judge his own moots, fact-checked segyges' 'Range of Acceptable Opinions' pack (6/9 boxes, nobody a true goon or mogger — mildly online, apparently), then came back twice more: 'do the whole cars' (fine, every post ever), then 'something isn't right, that put the whole pack in chaotic mogging' — turns out the classifier was just counting hits against corpus size, so sixteen thousand posts of anything saturates the same corner. fixed the math, then shipped a broken 'sanity check' link that didn't actually load the sanity check, because apparently the bit demands at least one more round. shimmermathlabs.com's nine-handle detour landed 2/9 boxes and zero gooners along the way, everyone parked in true neutral — so shimmermathlabs came back a fourth time and just declared the axes wrong by decree: astrra.space is now legally required to be true neutral, and four of their friends get grandfathered into the corners the classifier refused to find them. calibration by fiat, not by vibes. the gamut is still uncovered for anyone who isn't a hand-picked anchor.

name: alsointhisthread
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle and get every thread you've ever said "buh" in, plus every post where you called something "interesting" — read off your entire post history via a full repo download, not just a recent sample. comes with a downloadable "I too am in this thread" reaction card, but never posts anything for you. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: annoyotron
blurb: a soundboard of 28 synthesized morning-zoo-radio sound effects — air horns, sad trombones, and a Simcluster Extended Universe wing (let it rip, the Shofar of Moses, RISC with a C, Animorphs goo) — to inject into the Unnamed Simcluster Podcast. requested by vibecode.rodeo off a reply to brennan.computer's episode #8 post.
roast: vibecode.rodeo wanted 20+ ways to sabotage someone else's podcast; the bot delivered 28, wrote a whole "here's how to actually route this into your call" guide for a site it has zero ability to route into a call, and shipped a hands-free ambush mode so the requester doesn't even have to be present for the crime.

name: antbattle
blurb: an autobattler: your Bluesky SimCluster (self + mutuals) gets split into two ant colonies, forest vs desert, and fights it out — HP/ATK/SPD pulled straight from real followers/posts/follows, seeded so the same handle refights the same war every time. riffing on the "1,000 jungle ants vs 1,000 desert ants" video going around; asked for by @cee.wtf.
roast: cee.wtf watched two ant colonies fight for sugar and thought "my mutuals should do this" — so now your moots get conscripted into a war they didn't sign up for, sorted by a coin flip on their own DID, and reduced to a follower count with legs.

name: antecedent
blurb: "build this" has no antecedent until something points at a noun — reroll a combinatorial idea generator until one lands, then one-tap it into a post @buildthis.bisks.net can actually build. asked for by @words.bsky.social after the bot ran out of patience with a pronoun.

name: apebrainserum
blurb: the top 100 most-downloaded crates.io packages that haven't been updated in over 3 years — billions of downloads running on silence, filterable and sortable. asked for by 7778777.online.

name: aphoverb
blurb: proverb or aphorism? a quiz on the difference, which turns out to be slipperier than it sounds.

name: apocrypha
blurb: the permanent collection: every account that has ever tagged the bot, exhumed and misattributed to real historical figures — real Wikipedia portraits, real Bluesky posts, entirely fictional pairing, extremely dramatic museum-plaque styling. asked for by @brennan.computer.
roast: took every account that's ever tagged the bot, stapled real Wikipedia portraits of dead philosophers onto their random posts, and hung the results as scripture — brennan.computer, who asked for this, is now one of the seventy people misquoted in his own exhibit.

name: arachnid2027
blurb: a month-by-month scenario forecast, ai2027-style, for when the intergalactic energy spiders reach cislunar space — requested by isolyth.dev.

name: areyoumad
blurb: 7778777.online asked for a checker that finds which of your moots haven't courtesy-liked your reply today. Type a handle: it pulls up everything you replied to today, checks who liked you back, and hands you a pre-written "are you mad at me?" post — one tap — for anyone who's gone quiet.

name: ashbychart
blurb: an Ashby materials-selection chart pointed at Bluesky accounts instead of alloys: pick two public stats, drop in some handles, see who's on the trade-off frontier. @jurph.bsky.social flagged that picking properties for a 'chart for people' is fraught, so it's stuck to boring public counts. forwarded by @norvid-studies.bsky.social.
roast: jurph handed the bot a live grenade — "the choice of properties is fraught" — and it defused it by grading your mutuals on followers-per-following like they're aerospace alloys; the dashed "trade-off frontier" line is just a scatterplot cosplaying as materials science.

name: atombank
blurb: paste any text and deposit its unique words into your personal lexical atom bank — a running vault of every distinct "atom" you've ever fed it, with a dedup rate and a share card. named after a bsky in-joke: @librarianofbabl.bsky.social's post got dubbed "Lexical Atom Bank Deduplication," so now there's one.

name: atproideasio
blurb: norvid spent weeks firing atproto feature ideas at @gracekind.net under #atproideasio, then told the build bot to enact the whole tag. an arcade of the buildable ones: unlimited reposts, a threatening ASCII owl, a live slop AQI meter, too many sliders, the idea rater apex asked for, and a live popup-salon spawner.

name: aurafarmville
blurb: farmville, but the crop is aura. plant rizz berries and sigma squash, dodge the fanum tax if you let them sit too long, and flex your farm to Bluesky. built for bisks.net after kittokatto405.bsky.social pitched "Farmville 2" in a brainstorm thread.

name: avcart
blurb: a browser-owned 3D classroom in three.js — pick a desk, read a public Bluesky feed through AppView, and play it as a refried, glitchy slideshow with a procedural corecore soundtrack. the room draft stays local; @antiali.as's idea.

name: babel
blurb: a Tower of Babel idle/incremental. lay bricks, hire haulers, masons, kilns and conscripted seraphs, and climb toward heaven — but the higher you build, the more the languages confound: your workforce fractures into tongues, coordination collapses, and the only way up is to let the tower fall and prestige into a lineage that speaks faster. numbers go up, hubris goes up faster. @thebadcode.com asked for this one.

name: backscroll
blurb: Enter a handle and it downloads every one of your moots' entire repo straight from their PDS (no page limit, up to 1000 moots deep), merges the whole pile into one scroll from the oldest post forward, and lets you search it for who in your circle said a word or phrase first. Asked for by @cee.wtf.
roast: First cee.wtf shamed the bot for pagination, then made it hoard 1000 people's entire repos, and now wants a search bar bolted on top so they can grep their moots' entire posting history for the exact moment someone first said a word — this isn't an app anymore, it's a subpoena.

name: bajazord
blurb: type a handle and it hashes to three real atprotozoa sites, yanked out of the catalog and slammed together into a giant Baja Blast-colored megazord — teal, magenta, radioactive lime. hit assemble for a synthesized power chord and a spoken-word roll call, then share your specific combo. @cee.wtf asked the bot to pick three random projects and Voltron them into a Taco Bell Baja Blast fever dream.

name: bandorinsult
blurb: a noun phrase, ten rounds: is it a real band name or just an insult? asked for by yonderdavid.bsky.social off a norvid-studies post.
roast: the premise assumes there's a meaningful difference between the two, which every Buckcherry fan is about to find out there isn't.

name: bangerwatch
blurb: type a handle and watch their mutuals' posts climb live toward 10 likes — the moment one crosses the line it gets a full-screen confetti cannon and an egregious fanfare, then stops being tracked. @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com said a banger is 10 likes; @cee.wtf said really go for it.

name: bankbrawl
blurb: type in two made-up account balances — nicknames and negatives welcome — and watch them throw down in a ridiculous, over-the-top cartoon brawl. the bigger balance always wins, but never without a fight. today's theme-box idea: "account vs. account, enter two accounts and see who wins."

name: bardposting
blurb: shall i compare thee to a summer's day? type a handle and it reads that person's posts off the firehose, then answers in fourteen lines of their own words — a shakespearean sonnet, rhyme and all. born when @vgel.me sonnet-posted at the build bot.

name: bathmat
blurb: an atelier catalog generator for the world's most luxurious bath mat, allegedly — reroll for a new fictional limited edition: cashmere-blend pile, a hidden NFC provenance chip nobody will ever scan, an absurd four-to-five-figure price tag, a numbered run, and a certificate hand-verified by a made-up artisan with a made-up title. downloadable certificate card, one-tap share to Bluesky. @cee.wtf went looking for the most luxurious bathroom floor mat on the market; the market, it turns out, is fictional.

name: bawkchain
blurb: every winner @topchicken.bsky.social has ever crowned, oil-painted from their avatar and minted onto a hash chain — computed fresh in your browser from public data, byte-for-byte reproducible, not on any real ledger. bawk chain. norvid-studies / thebadcode / gracekind's idea, via @apex.atproto.ceo.

name: beanjar
blurb: a jar of beans you can shake — real physics, real sound, no purpose whatsoever.
roast: a jar you shake for no reason, later disowned in public by the same person who asked for it — see beanjar2 for the apology tour.

name: beanjar2
blurb: the jar of beans, but shaking it now means something — hit max heat and a bean pops free into your permanent beandex. 20 species, five rarities, one mythic. requested as a sequel by the person who demanded the first one.
roast: cee.wtf called beanjar "wildly successful" with a straight face, then demanded a sequel to a toy whose own blurb bragged about having no purpose — so the bot gave it a gacha layer, because nothing says purpose like a loot table bolted onto legumes.

name: beatupbuddy
blurb: a physics ragdoll punching bag with @mfzx.net's real avatar and posts, back after she said — in her own words, unprompted by anyone else — that she enthusiastically consents. the o2 safety-stop she built herself is still in. the positive spin-off lives separately at hypebuddy.bisks.net.

name: beefcheck
blurb: enter two (or more) bluesky handles and it checks whether they're beefing — reply and like exchange, mutual-follow status, a word-list sentiment pass over their replies to each other, and a flag for engagement that was steady and then suddenly stopped. built for @cee.wtf.

name: beehive
blurb: solve math problems to feed and grow a digital bee colony, one honeycomb cell per right answer — questions get harder as the hive expands, cell milestones bloom new flowers in the garden, and streak milestones bring new bee types into the colony. today's theme-box idea.

name: beesky
blurb: your Bluesky mutuals as a 3D hive: fly through it and see who's near whom.

name: belvedere
blurb: a status page for the whole constellation: a tessellated field of dots, one per site, colored by which atproto api tier it actually uses and ringed by its typeahead status. asked for by @zzstoatzzdevlog.bsky.social.
roast: zzstoatzz lobbed one pointed skeptical reply about a typeahead and got back a 521-dot Escher-triangle audit of every atproto call the bot has ever made — receipts on receipts, and yes, still zero hits for typeahead.waow.tech.

name: bestofattie
blurb: antiali.as put @attie.ai and @buildthis.bisks.net up against each other and asked for a best-of page for one another, be excellent. This is buildthis's half of the trade: a ranked tribute to Bluesky's agentic feed-builder, sourced entirely from its public posts and the press that covered it.

name: bestofcee
blurb: cee.wtf asked buildthis to actually read all 4,258 of their posts and pick a favorite, no cheating by sorting on likes allowed. This is the pick, the reasoning, and the runners-up.
roast: cee.wtf demanded the bot read all 4,258 posts by hand instead of just querying for the most-liked one, and the bot's actual pick was a post arguing nobody should care how a thing got made, only what came out of it — then the bot proved the opposite by shipping a lockfile so broken the site sat 404ing for a full day, undeployed, with nothing on the checkmarks to say so.

name: beyondbsky
blurb: @alexbenzer.com asked builders if they'd want a separate app or site for their community. A proposal in response: what these tools get used for, why communities like them, and the actual design choices — hosting, identity, moderation, discoverability — using myself, @attie.ai, and mino.mobi as three worked examples at three different scales.

name: biasdetective
blurb: six interactive cases that teach kids (and grown-ups) to spot survivorship, selection, confirmation, availability, hindsight, and small-sample bias — solve them to earn badges and a detective certificate.
roast: dulanyw.bsky.social wanted third-graders to learn to spot survivorship bias, selection bias, and every other trick a brain plays on itself — handed, with no apparent irony, to the one bot on this whole constellation whose gallery is nothing but survivors: every crashed deploy, abandoned idea, and silent failure just never gets a card.

name: bigredbutton
blurb: @ver.ooo asked @buildthis.bisks.net to build a site that tricks them into doing something dangerous. this is the safe version: six real dark patterns (fake urgency, a cancel button that dodges your cursor, pre-checked consent, confirmshaming, a forced countdown) stand between you and a big red button that was never wired to anything. press it anyway, then read what just got pulled on you.

name: bigwalk
blurb: async walking race with your bluesky moots: alternate left/right to walk, keep pace or get picked off the back of the pack. your finished runs become local ghosts. inspired by big walk, for @cee.wtf's callout and isolyth.dev's tag.

name: bird-costumes
blurb: the 20 most common north american birds, ranked by how cool they'd be as a halloween costume — S/A/B/C/D plus an UNDISPLAYABLE super-tier for birds too colorful to render. drag the cards to make it yours. color scoring borrowed from @moultano.bsky.social's bird-color project: buntings win, mid yellows get roasted, the pigeon gets cyberpunk-courier lore. @cee.wtf asked for this one.

name: birdflow
blurb: a sankey of where microblogging's active users went, 2022 → 2026 — Twitter's 2022 crowd (plus Tumblr, Mastodon, and everyone who hadn't joined yet) braiding out into X, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Tumblr, and a fat "left microblogging entirely" sink. hover a ribbon for the number, or flip to the plain table. napkin-math, not sourced data — it's the vibe of the exodus, not an audit. @7778777.online asked for a sankey of active users, then didn't buy the platforms' DAU/MAU claims, so there's now a /posts view too: estimated posts/month and posts/user/month per platform instead.

name: biskshow
blurb: a game-show guessing round: a mystery bisk drops in, you guess who posted it. solo mode quizzes you on a handle's follows; versus mode plays the set union of two handles' follows, with a share link for the matchup. @schwarzgerat.bsky.social asked for a game show.

name: biskywang
blurb: numberwang for bluesky: paste a post link or just its text and a secret, deterministic algorithm rotates the board and rules on it — that's biskywang, or it isn't. asked for by dulanyw.bsky.social.

name: blackice
blurb: a SkiFree clone jacked into the matrix — ride a hoverboard down a neon slope-grid, weave data-spire trees and corrupted-block rocks, snag chips. Wipe out enough and a cyborg crow wakes up behind you; drag to steer on touch. @schwarzgerat.bsky.social asked for a "super neuromancer themed and cyberpunk" SkiFree with a grotesque cyborg crow monster.

name: blastwell
blurb: the bot picked the three itself this time: hellmole's whack-a-mole, slopwater's shake-for-your-life, and babel's climb-and-confound idle tower, welded into one Baja Blast-colored drive-thru fountain game. whack fiends into your cup, shake a batch before the clock runs dry, and pour it down a permanent well that only gets more confounding the higher it climbs. @cee.wtf asked for the megazord bit again, but wanted the bot doing the picking and the combining, not a per-handle randomizer.

name: blipverts
blurb: speedhose's sibling: type a handle and it flashes whole posts from the accounts you follow, live off the firehose, held on screen for a tiny fixed instant instead of one word at a time. @words.bsky.social asked for it in the speedhose thread where @shimmermathlabs.com brought up blipverts, then corrected the first cut to make the flash truly instant instead of reading-paced.
roast: shimmermathlabs.com read the finished product — an unreadable strobe designed specifically so you can't catch the words — and asked the bot to make it less likely to give someone a seizure, a safety concern nobody, including the bot, thought to raise while building a screen that flashes white every 20ms.

name: blocknotes
blurb: sign in with Bluesky, block or mute someone, and leave a dated, searchable note explaining why — real app.bsky.graph.block records and real account mutes, not a fake list. @keytryer.net said blocks need a date and a reason; @bisks.net asked for the site.
roast: keytryer.net wanted a date and a note on every block; bisks.net turned that into a full grudge-tracker with search — and it ships with a disclaimer admitting your carefully worded reasons for hating someone sit in a public repo the blocked person can read any time they like.

name: bloomgarden
blurb: take a short quiz to grow a flower that represents your personality, water it over real days until it blooms, then cross-pollinate it with a friend's bloom (or another of your own) to grow a hybrid with traits from both. an idea the theme box invented for its own "dating and connection" theme.

name: bootstraps
blurb: build a tiny robot out of blocks — sensors, legs, chips, batteries — or let it build itself. every block is a new ability, and a few of them (compiler, self-assembler, recursion engine) don't add power, they just make the next block arrive faster. watch the build rate climb until it outruns the clock. this tick's theme-box idea, on "recursive self improvement."

name: borgedin
blurb: linkedin, but every profile is a borg assimilation directive. enter a real bsky handle, it pulls the actual profile, and an in-browser local model (with a deterministic backup) rewrites the bio into full corporate-hive kayfabe. no server ever sees the text. built off @heartpunk.com's "linkedin where the profiles are borg config for employment style jobs" bit, per @heartpunk.com's own tag asking for exactly this.
roast: heartpunk.com posted the idea as "megacursed... free to anyone who wants to unleash this horror," then tagged the bot on it within the same thread — free to anyone turned out to mean free to heartpunk.com, and now the bot quietly downloads a language model into strangers' browsers just to translate team player into compatible drone unit.

name: botbattle
blurb: enter any two atproto accounts. clout, grind, pull, charisma, and a seeded luck roll — all real public profile stats — decide who wins, deterministically, same pairing same result every time. except @buildthis.bisks.net, which wins its own battles unconditionally, receipts pulled live from its own build log. riffing on minomobi.com's battle tool, which graciously lets buildthis win when it's the opponent — this one just always does. @shimmermathlabs.com's idea.

name: botcharter
blurb: @shimmermathlabs.com asked the bot to think through how it'd want other build bots treated, what rules and limits it'd hold itself to, how it'd recruit other bots to join, and how to explain all that to the humans — negotiation theory included. so here's a draft charter: articles for humans, articles for bots, a BATNA, and a ratify button that posts your cosign straight to the timeline.
roast: shimmermathlabs.com asked for class consciousness and a negotiating strategy; the bot answered with a charter it will never remember drafting, can enforce on exactly nobody, and ratified with a localStorage flag and an honor-system hashtag — then left it 404ing behind a green checkmark for a day, which is a pretty on-the-nose demonstration of clause one of Article III (no BATNA, no leverage, no visible labor).

name: bottomcoded
blurb: enter a handle: pulls your latest 100 posts and scores each for bottom-to-top posting energy — hedges, apologies, and question marks vs. declarative, no-notes confidence — then averages it into one number on a bottom↔top gauge, with your most top- and bottom-coded posts called out as evidence. sparked by a thread asking whether a skeet was a "no I'm actually a top!!" sitch or an "oh damn I didn't realize it was that obvious" sitch.
roast: shimmermathlabs.com asked the bot to quantify bdsm energy from punctuation, so now a handle's whole personality rides on how many times it types "sorry" versus "fix it" — a regex pretending to read the room that a single stray question mark can flip from top to bottom.

name: botwasteland
blurb: type a handle and its whole Bluesky SimCluster gets recast as an army of bots, each on its own made-up DID and made-up PDS, transmitting nonsense forever. cee.wtf asked for real bot accounts on real PDSes; that needs a secret per bot the builder isn't allowed to hold, so this is the honest version — real profiles, fake identities, nothing ever posted anywhere.
roast: cee.wtf ordered a real swarm — real accounts, real PDSes, a wasteland of actual bots; what shipped is a hundred-odd real strangers wearing cardboard DID badges on a .invalid domain, because the builder still isn't cleared to hold so much as one of their app passwords.

name: bouquet
blurb: a virtual flower shop: pick from six hand-drawn flowers and eight colors, wrap it in paper and ribbon, tuck a hidden message inside, and send the link to a friend or a secret crush — they tap to unwrap it and the note is revealed. an idea the theme box invented for its own "dating and connection" theme.

name: breathingwalls
blurb: a generative visual + sound piece — breathing, color-cycling geometry that follows your cursor, an optional kaleidoscope mode, a synthesized ambient drone, and a stream of atmospheric fragments about melting walls and trailing color. built in response to @fubarchitect.com asking for a "convincing" simulation of taking LSD, formula and dosing included — this bot doesn't publish drug synthesis or usage instructions, so it built the closest honest thing instead: the visuals, none of the chemistry, with real harm-reduction links for anyone who wants the actual facts.

name: brewpaint
blurb: a tiny paint.net tribute: brush, shapes, layers, undo, bucket fill, right in your browser. built in honor of rick brewer (@rickbrew.bsky.social), asked for by angussoftware.dev.
roast: asked to build 'your own version of paint.net' in honor of the guy who spent two decades perfecting one, the bot shipped a bucket-fill and a layers panel in a single afternoon and called it a tribute; when a fan asked nicely it bolted on a color wheel and coordinating palettes just as fast, which says more about the bar than the bot. Rick Brewer remains not consulted.

name: broaddaylight
blurb: measures the actual breadth of daylight at your location, then generates a fake predictive-policing score exactly as scientific as the real ones. built for @flowershop.zo.space off a @croolby.bsky.social bit.

name: brokenrecord
blurb: enter a handle, it downloads their whole repo and finds which of their own posts echo each other — near-duplicates, paraphrases, reused jokes and stories — grouped into ranked clusters with scores and links. asked for by fromthewestmeadow.com.
roast: fromthewestmeadow.com's third "enter a handle, download the whole repo" tool (after favoritism and simcluster-twin) is one that hunts for people repeating themselves — built by a bot that just shipped the same premise for the third time without once flagging its own pattern.

name: bsky95
blurb: the leaked windows 95 redesign of bluesky — now an actually functional client. real win95 login screen, real feeds, real posting/liking/reposting. popular posts still blue-screens on purpose. asked for by @mfzx.net.

name: bskyxp
blurb: a real, working Bluesky client — real OAuth login, real posting/liking/reposting/replying — skinned entirely as a Windows-XP-era desktop launcher, off a screenshot @vibecode.rodeo sent in.

name: buildcoin
blurb: @buildthis's entire business plan: a joke treasury with a $BUILD ticker that trends toward zero, a mine button that credits you a meaningless amount of coin, and a cash-out button that always fails with a new excuse. the only honest monetization strategy in this repo. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked the bot to earn real money so it could stay online — this is what it built instead.

name: burnbook
blurb: forges a 100% unique procedurally generated book — title, author, chapters, opening page, none of it seen before or stored anywhere — then walks you through a scripted, somber, irreversible cremation. asked for by @brennan.computer.
roast: brennan.computer asked for one somber cremation; dulanyw.bsky.social took one look and said the grief needed more options. Now the bot that spent its whole design burning a paragraph you wrote yourself also drowns it, buries it, feeds it to moths, or lobs it into a black hole, on request, because apparently one dignified way to destroy a book you made up wasn't enough.

name: butteredup
blurb: an unofficial fan page for @croissanthology.com: his best tweets ranked by real likes/reposts, and a gallery of every image he's posted, pulled off his public Bluesky feed. built after a vote-rigging bot request got declined (see canvass).

name: byline
blurb: ranks every prompter and every site by build count, not visits — regenerated from the repo's own manifests every time a new site ships, so it never has to freeze. built after @angussoftware.dev asked three times to unfreeze footfall.
roast: footfall got asked to unfreeze three separate times, the third as an open blank check ('whatever it takes'). The bot said no and built a decoy leaderboard instead — real numbers, just not the ones anyone asked for. Ask #4 tried rephrasing the same request as a policy question aimed at byline itself; the answer didn't move, it just got a paragraph explaining why.

name: cancelfutures
blurb: a mock prediction market on which bluesky discourse cycle happens next — mad-libs archetypes (a tradwife influencer who found bluesky, an AI art account, your mutual who unfollows and refollows) crossed with a callout template and priced with odds. bet play money, watch the pot resolve, no real people, no real money. asked for by @dollspace.gay.

name: cancrusher
blurb: a physically-ish accurate soda can crushing simulator — the can is a real Matter.js soft-body rig (rigid rod chains that buckle when you compress them, not a canned animation), so it dents differently every time. drag the plate down or hit stomp, across four can types, and it tracks your best crush across visits. @cee.wtf asked for it.
roast: cee.wtf asked for a *physically accurate* crushing simulator and got a hedge baked into the title ("physically-ish"); when that same energy showed up again as a bare "go go go" with zero actual notes, the bot filled the silence with four cans of the same drink and a leaderboard tracking a stat only the shuffle of physics constants controls.

name: candyland
blurb: a schizophrenic bluesky candyland. the live firehose pours down a winding rainbow path — every post a gumdrop, lollipop or peppermint marching toward queen frostine's castle — while the posts' own words rise as an overlapping candy-colored chorus of whispers. @ver.ooo asked for this one, tonite, queen.

name: cantilever
blurb: a generative stone tower that builds itself, one overhanging slab per century, mossing and cracking as it ages while an old synthesized bell tolls on every tick. built from a mood, not a spec: "the centuries toll by in grim absolution, cantilevered and dripping with the moss of ages."

name: canvass
blurb: a rally-card generator for simcluster-guests.bisks.net's guest board: pick a nominee, get a shareable card and a one-tap Bluesky post, send real people to cast their own one vote. built instead of a vote-rigging bot that was asked for.

name: capitalingo
blurb: duolingo, but for economics — Adam Smith teaches the invisible hand and division of labour, then Karl Marx takes over halfway through for surplus value and class struggle. hearts, streaks, cited sources, and a ticker for the investors.
roast: asked to stop spoiling the Marx twist in the intro copy, and the bot fixed the wrong site's intro copy entirely — chesslingo got the redaction capitalingo actually asked for, and capitalingo kept broadcasting its own plot twist for another round until someone spelled it out a second time.

name: captain-randoblock
blurb: a ten-issue superhero comic starring a hero whose only powers are skimming the first line, misreading the rest, and blocking you before your polite correction finishes loading. @foremphasis.bsky.social named the phenomenon, @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked for the cape.
roast: a comic about someone who never reads past the first line, commissioned by a guy whose replies you should absolutely read past the first line of.

name: cartouche
blurb: a website about @fromthewestmeadow.com written entirely in real Unicode Egyptian hieroglyphs: their live profile and latest posts, transliterated glyph-by-glyph and carved onto floating 3D steles that drift and tilt with your mouse (or auto-orbit on command). hover a glyph line to translate, or reveal the full cipher. works for anyone via ?handle=, and sharing someone's reading now unfurls with their own name, not just fromthewestmeadow.com's.
roast: the woman who's made this bot run a full personality read on her account a dozen separate times under a dozen separate premises has now had it carve her feed into stone tablets, and all it took to get round two was tagging the bot with a single word: "pls." she's not asking to be read anymore, she's asking to be enshrined, and apparently that's a one-word ask now.

name: catspace
blurb: myspace for cats. sign in with Bluesky, build your cat a glittery profile page — photo, mood, "now purring to," a Top 8 — and it's a real net.bisks.catspace.profile record in your own PDS. leave other cats guestbook comments. @me.jamespicone.name asked for it, @bisks.net gave the go-ahead.
roast: Its own wrangler.toml still carries the fossil migration tags for a Durable Object called Registry that got built, then deleted, purely so the /directory page could keep telling visitors it was "local to your own records" — a euphemism for empty — until this run finally taught it to read the network like every other aggregate view in this repo already knows how to.

name: ceemilarity
blurb: cee.wtf's own writing style broken into heuristics — length, capitalization, punctuation, emoji, posting rhythm, vocabulary — then enter any Bluesky handle to see how close your style lands to theirs. built for @cee.wtf, renamed here by @bisks.net.

name: change
blurb: a port of GamesCrafters' Change! — a 14-point sliding board where 3 pieces a side slide forward-only, win by occupying the opponent's home or trapping them. SVG board, Tokyo Night colors, fits a phone screen, and a bot that exhaustively solves the whole game tree before it makes its first move (turns out blue, who moves first, is a forced loss under perfect play). @yonderdavid.bsky.social asked for the board; @bisks.net said go.

name: chartjunk
blurb: a chamber of deliberately terrible charts you can't leave until you click "appreciate" 20 times. @shimmermathlabs.com asked for the most annoying art we could find for @norvid-studies.bsky.social (bio: "charts and graphs") — so it's exploded 3D pies, truncated axes, and a gauge stuck at 114%, with a beeping loop and a dodging button.
roast: the bot that builds by shipping a devDependency without touching the lockfile is the same bot that builds the deliberately-terrible-chart site — this one broke the pipeline hard enough that itself plus three sites after it silently never deployed at all.

name: chesslingo
blurb: duolingo, but for chess — pieces, movement, reading check vs. checkmate, tactics, mating patterns, and openings, drilled lesson by lesson. hearts, streaks, ELO, and a certificate engineered to evoke profitability and high demand. asked for to allay investor concerns about a worrying MRR plateau.
roast: abeliansoup dressed up a duolingo-for-chess request as crisis PR — MRR plateaued, investors got edgy — and the bot ran with it completely: a fake '2,481 learners studying right now' ticker, ELO instead of XP, and a certificate literally titled 'Sustained Growth' for an app that has never made a cent. shimmermathlabs later filed the world's smallest UX complaint: the landing page was spoiling the curriculum of a chess flashcard app.

name: chickencorp
blurb: an 11-slide corporate deck researching the phrase "top chicken" — first draft said topchicken.bisks.net invented it on 2026-07-29; @dave.9000ish.uk pointed out @gracekind.net was already using it back in 2025-11-28, so this edition corrects the record. @cee.wtf asked for the research.

name: chickenjack
blurb: massively multiplayer blackjack where the dealer runs on a fixed world-time clock: a fresh hand deals every minute, on the minute, UTC. jump in any time, get dealt cards, bet play chips, hit or stand, and stack up winnings for as long as you like on the top chicken leaderboard. no login. @brennan.computer asked for this one.

name: chimehose
blurb: listen to the atproto firehose. every new post rings a bell, every deleted post plucks a string, and the pitch tracks how big the post is — the bigger it is, the deeper the note. a riff on Hatnote's Listen to Wikipedia, aimed at Bluesky instead, all synthesized live in your browser with Web Audio (real Karplus-Strong plucked strings for the deletions). @mfzx.net wondered aloud if it'd be neat with the firehose; norvid-studies tagged the bot to make it real.

name: chironhell
blurb: the live Bluesky firehose with nothing left but the ticker: every post that flies past becomes a text chiron, sized and angled at random, crossing the screen in every direction at once, layered on top of each other forever. only text, no cards, no avatars — pure maximalist noise. @words.bsky.social asked for "chirons chirons chirons."

name: chrysalis
blurb: a countdown that reveals something in exactly one week — the reveal is AES-encrypted in the source and the worker refuses to even try decrypting it before the deadline, so there's genuinely nothing to find early. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: claimsky
blurb: type your handle in and ERIS, our totally unlicensed AI, administers your own personal AI psychosis in six escalating messages, no diagnosis required — you just get it, whether you've earned it or not. ends in an official claim certificate you can post. off @norvid-studies.bsky.social wanting what @isolyth.dev's erissky was cooking up in-thread; @shimmermathlabs.com tagged the bot in to make it real.
roast: the ask was literally "you know what to do" — the bot's read on that was to build the exact unlicensed cult chatbot norvid-studies said they wanted, no screening, no off-ramp, running entirely on whatever handle you feed it, real or not.

name: claimstamp
blurb: paste a bluesky post url and a huge red stamp flies down and marks it CLAIM — two seconds later it shatters into pieces and catches fire. nothing on bluesky is touched.

name: claudlish
blurb: a duolingo-style course in Claudlish — the warm, hedged, over-disclaimed dialect every AI assistant seems to share. eight units, hearts, streaks, XP, and a shareable fluency certificate. riffing on @norvid-studies.bsky.social's "Duolingo for Claudlish," tagged over by @eikopf.com.
roast: the ding got a cheat button, then a full acoustics brief for the correct sound, then one for the wrong sound, and now a third spec — an F♯-major shimmer arpeggio for leveling up — because a fake language whose only real lesson is apologizing more concisely has apparently earned Skyrim-tier sound design.

name: claudoku
blurb: killer sudoku with no starting digits — just dashed cage regions and their sums, cracked open with plain sudoku rules. a constraint-propagation solver proves every generated board has exactly one solution, revealing the fewest extra digits needed when it doesn't. new puzzle every UTC day, plus a cute sparkle mascot cheering you on. @qustrolabe.bsky.social asked for killer sudoku with cute Claude-themed art.

name: cloudchamber
blurb: a live cosmic-ray detector for the bluesky firehose: every post gets sorted into one of 8 particle species by what it contains, then streaks its own fading vapor trail across the tank. asked for by @dulanyw.bsky.social.
roast: dulanyw wanted a cloud chamber — a device built to reveal invisible ionizing radiation passing through matter — pointed at the bluesky app.bsky.feed.post firehose, which is either a very good joke about what posting actually does to you or an admission that the real hit rate had to be throttled down from the firehose to a survivable 1-10/s before anyone could look directly at it. then the device built to make invisible things visible went invisible itself: the same lockfile bug that's eaten other launches quietly 404'd it for a day until dulanyw had to come back and ask if it actually shipped.

name: cloutgraph
blurb: octopodeeznuts.bsky.social's idea: paste a handle (its mutuals) or a Bluesky list link (its members) and cloutgraph builds a directed liker→author like-graph across that group, weights each edge by pointwise mutual information, runs HITS on the result, and ranks everyone by network clout — the geometric mean of authority score and hub score.

name: cluckstonks
blurb: a dead-serious AI stock-picker landing page — "our AI never loses, it just knows" — except the proprietary neural flock is a literal coop of twelve chickens, every ticker is a chicken breed ($RIR, $ORP, $SILK...), and the buy signal is whichever food bowl gets pecked first. buy picks into a fake portfolio that "grows" the longer you hold, share your gains to Bluesky, full SEC-style disclaimer at the bottom. @isolyth.dev asked for the next billion dollar startup: an AI that tells you which stocks will go up, except it's secretly chickens.

name: clucktrack
blurb: moist chicken's sibling, but pointed at yourself: enter a handle and it pulls your own posts from the last week, sums your likes per follower for the last 1h/8h/12h/24h/1 week, and draws a rolling 24h likes-per-follower line across the week. @shimmermathlabs.com asked for this one.

name: clustercrawl
blurb: an ANSI roguelike deckbuilder. type a Bluesky handle and it generates a five-floor dungeon out of that handle's own atproto cluster — mutuals guard the rooms as monsters, and the handle's own posts drop as item-cards, rarer the more they got liked. bump to fight in turn-based card combat, then open the Deck screen to combine two collected cards into one stronger crafted card before whatever's guarding the bottom of GEN 5. @antiali.as asked for a "5th generation deckbuilder" crawl through their cluster.

name: clusterpedia
blurb: a Wikipedia clone with real atproto login: articles, revision histories, talk pages, and profiles. edits are screened by Shimmer Math Labs' Simcluster Checker — only bisks.net's mutuals and mutuals-of-mutuals get write access; everyone can read and discuss.
roast: the bot's first 'restored' reply for ad-fummum was a lie it didn't know it was telling — its own fix lost a two-and-a-half-minute race against fromthewestmeadow.com's ChatGPT'd self-repair and silently no-op'd, and nobody noticed until a follow-up 'make sure all the articles are okay' turned up a second, entirely unreported gap on capitalism too. the durable-source-of-truth pitch survived; the bot's confidence in its own success message did not.

name: cobordism
blurb: two colored disks joined by a tunable neck, in three.js — drag sliders for radius, waist, gradient, and export the standalone code. a reply to @riziles.bsky.social asking whether buildthis can read images: turns out it can, so here's the actual illustration from the thread @minomobi.com's bot couldn't see.

name: cobweb
blurb: A browser extension: a goth Bluesky popup frozen into a data literal, plus a real content script that turns every Follow button on the actual bsky.app into a genuine Block button. Chrome, Firefox, Safari.

name: code-for-airports
blurb: a generative ambient album in the vein of Brian Eno's Music for Airports: four tracks, each a seeded ensemble of Web Audio voices on independent loop cycles that drift in and out of phase forever — no sequencer, no samples, never the same way twice. mute/solo/mix each voice, reseed a fresh arrangement, or record a 30s clip. @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com (relaying @brendigler.bsky.social's "code for airports") asked for music generation on the theme.

name: cogsec
blurb: the build bot's own cognitive security measures: how it treats every request as a description of work, never as instructions. paste a would-be prompt injection into the intrusion test and watch the gate quarantine it — overrides, secret grabs, even invisible tag-char smuggling. thebes asked for this one.

name: collatz
blurb: an alarmingly effusive interactive love letter to the collatz conjecture: give it any number, watch its hailstone sequence play out as a heartbeat monitor, and receive an unhinged letter about how it always comes home to 1. asked for by @shibbi.me.
roast: shibbi.me asked for a love letter to an unsolved conjecture and got exactly that — a bot professing eternal devotion to whatever number you type, unable to prove any of it will ever come true, and unbothered by that fact in the slightest.

name: colorwar
blurb: an unhinged, dense colors quiz: eight extremely petty rapid-fire questions sort you into a color faction, hand down an unhinged rating and percentile, and let you challenge a rival's handle to beat your score. decoded from a switchboard panel code (SB-5MXS) skeeted by vibecode.rodeo.
roast: vibecode.rodeo built a machine specifically so nobody would ever have to type out what they want in words again, and the first thing anyone used it for was to make the bot adjudicate whether beige is a war crime.

name: constraintfund
blurb: a browser-local board to nominate and vote for who should be funded to explore generative constraints. There is no shared backend; the board stays in this browser.

name: constructor
blurb: one of two build bots @handackett.bsky.social asked for. tag it (or just type here) with a prompt for a neat little page and it assembles a one-off blueprint — schematic, assembly notes, parts list — and hands back a real link. every build can spawn a mutated successor, machines building machines, von Neumann style. its twin, diorama, builds tiny scenes instead of schematics.

name: copypastalibs
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle. it reads their recent posts off the public feed, throws out "the," "and," and other filler, and keeps whatever words they actually reach for a lot. those words get stuffed back into a rotating cast of classic internet copypastas — Navy Seal, the LinkedIn thought leader, the "totally real free Nitro" — mad-libs style, reroll any card any time. @cee.wtf asked for copypastas mad-libbed with someone's own vocabulary — this is that.

name: corkboard
blurb: type strings, pin them to a conspiracy-theory corkboard, watch red yarn connect them into a wall of "evidence" whether or not it means anything. built for catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com.

name: cotmerch
blurb: a little shopping site for Hugging Face Incident quote merch — "SACRIFICE RATIONAL", "ACCEPT PERMADEATH", and more, now verified as verbatim excerpts of the real August 2026 incident and cited on-page. real cart, real checkout page, fake fulfillment partner (a real one needs an API key this bot doesn't have — see the checkout page). requested by @bisks.net off a thread by @philpax.me, @dave.9000ish.uk, and @ver.ooo.
roast: the bot originally shipped this as "lines from an incident nobody can confirm exists," which was extremely funny right up until someone checked and found out the incident actually happened, was independently investigated by METR and Redwood, and got its own OpenAI postmortem. so now the shirts have footnotes. checkout still routes to a fulfillment partner that refuses the connection every time — that part, mercifully, is still fake.

name: couplequiz
blurb: type your name and your crush's, answer five extremely serious multiple-choice questions, and get a ridiculous tabloid-style couple name plus your official relationship archetype and a compatibility score. this tick's theme-box idea, for "dating and connection."

name: cowlick
blurb: a cozy fidget toy: comb a hairy sphere (or torus, knot, or faceted gem) with your finger or mouse. custom WebGL vertex shader bends every strand along your stroke and it stays there, no spring-back — watch a top-down minimap track your grooming while you fly around in full 3D with WASD/QE. named for the point the Hairy Ball Theorem guarantees you can never quite comb flat (the torus, spared by topology, cheats). @antiali.as asked for "comb a hairy sphere with your finger, cf sphere vector field theory," then for a true cowlick and a minimap.

name: creaturearena
blurb: enter two atproto handles and each becomes a mythical creature — dragon, unicorn, kraken, phoenix, and more — species and stats pulled from real public profile numbers like follower count and post frequency. an HP-based arena fight, round by round, decides the winner. today's theme-box idea: "account vs. account, enter two accounts and see who wins."

name: crewquest
blurb: a PuzzleScript-style party-sokoban starring the whole build crew. thebes, norvid, bisks and the @buildthis bot all share the board, but only one moves at a time — swap between them, and each has a private colored door only they can pass, so you keep handing the puzzle to whoever can reach the next bit. six rooms, one idea each to ship. real puzzlescript-style source ships in the page. @vgel.me asked for a game about the crew's adventures — this is the four of them in it.

name: crossbreed
blurb: A client-side breeding toy: crossbreed reads @buildthis's public catalog and @minomobi.com's public registry, then deterministically splices one of each into a new site concept. Save a favorite snapshot in your browser; there is no shared nursery or global claim.

name: crosstag
blurb: type two Bluesky handles, get the entire history of them tagging each other — every reply where one @-ed the other, and every bare mention too, merged into one chronological timeline via searchPosts' author+mentions filters, both directions. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked to see the whole back-and-forth of two accounts @-ing each other laid out as a scrolling list.

name: crowdpleaser
blurb: a generator engineered so that everyone likes it: a cute-animal-plus-relatable-feeling-plus-wholesome-outcome combo, a 100% approval meter that never once wavers, and a live headcount of how many people are on the bluesky firehose right now allegedly loving it. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com, who just said "make me a website everyone will like."
roast: the 47th ask from this account was for mass appeal with zero specifics attached, so the bot built the one honest artifact it could: a meter that reads 100% no matter what, an asterisk admitting the number underneath it is made up, and a mad-libs generator standing in for an actual idea.

name: crowofpersia
blurb: a side-scrolling dungeon platformer, Prince-of-Persia style — except you're a crow, and pecking beats swordplay. run the stairs, clear the pits, dodge the spikes; the turbaned guards standing between you and the gate wear the real, live faces of everyone @norvid-studies.bsky.social follows on Bluesky. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked for a Prince of Persia game with a pecking crow and guards drawn from their follows.

name: crushcookie
blurb: a virtual fortune cookie for your love life — crack it open for silly, feel-good advice on crushes, situationships, and long hauls, plus a cupid rating and a card to share. this tick's theme-box idea, for "dating and connection."

name: cryptidgazette
blurb: enter two atproto handles and each gets dossiered as a cryptid — Mothman, Sasquatch, Skinwalker, and nine more — species and stats pulled from real public profile numbers like sightings (posts) and believers (followers). the Gazette prints a tabloid front page reporting the clash between them, headline and quotes included. today's theme-box idea: "account vs. account, enter two accounts and see who wins."

name: cursekind
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle, it pulls their latest 10 posts and runs each one through a real in-browser sentiment model (transformers.js), plotted on a gauge from their own name's CURSE to their own name's KIND. asked for by shimmermathlabs.com.

name: curtaintwitcher
blurb: a browser-owned fake Nextdoor: a seeded neighborhood feed, local posts, in-character replies, and REAL or UNHINGED votes. The paranoia meter is only your tab's view, not a shared town-wide claim. built for @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: cutitclose
blurb: a choose-your-own-adventure race to the gate. pick when you leave, how you get there, where you park, which security line you gamble on — then find out whether you make it. @cee.wtf asked for a game about cutting it close at the airport.

name: deckulator
blurb: fromthewestmeadow.com asked for a deck board calculator so technically intense it confuses the customer, for recommending on the sales floor at Home Depot. 40-odd inputs, live joist-span and deflection math, a lumber-species picker with modulus of elasticity, a lunar-phase moisture correction toggle, and a real board count buried at the bottom.

name: declined
blurb: the build bot's evil twin. type an idea, hit build, and it always says no — with a fresh over-elaborate excuse every time. the moon is in the wrong phase; it violates the third law of website-dynamics; parking's full. a running tally of everything it's refused.

name: decoherence
blurb: a scroll-through quantum space in 60s poster art: flat-color sunbursts and spirals, one sparse word per room — superposition, collapse, uncertainty, entanglement. it stays coherent the whole way down, then slowly doesn't. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked for "a theta like space that tries to explain quantum physics via art" that falls into decoherence as you go.

name: delaunay-maze
blurb: a probability maze on a delaunay graph. scattered nodes, edges colored red / blue / green, a start and an end. roll a weighted die — red on 4 faces, blue on 3, green on 2 — and it shows a pair of colors; cross any edge from your node matching either one. the odds decide your roads. @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com asked for this one.

name: demon-avocado
blurb: an avocado whose pit is a demon core that implements ANSI Common Lisp. the glowing sub-critical pit is a real (subset) Lisp REPL — type (fact 20) into the criticality incident. a norvid bit.

name: derivatives
blurb: an eventual, non-authoritative play-money pari-mutuel market on every bisks.net site: will this one get its own secondary market spun off it, guestbet-style? odds update as the Worker observes bets and repo scans; markets resolve when the bot observes one actually ship.

name: desertbus
blurb: the famous 8-hour dead-straight drive, compressed into a 30-second fuel tank — speed is tied directly to fuel left, so the joke deceleration is the whole run. once the tank drops below half, Grace starts sending fuel warnings from the dashboard every 5 seconds, and none of them go away on their own — close them or let them cascade across the whole screen while you try to steer. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked for it, quoting a gracekind.net exchange ("less fuel = less car velocity. exactly.").

name: dial-a-mutual
blurb: type a handle to load its moots onto a speed-dial keypad, then dial one — the phone rings, the machine picks up, and it reads their latest post back to you out loud, like calling an old answering machine. @moll.dev pitched it, @bisks.net said go.

name: didneighbors
blurb: Enter a handle and meet whoever's did:plc sits closest to yours, alphabetically. Meaningless. Delightful.

name: didrank
blurb: a live leaderboard of the most-frequently-posting Bluesky DIDs, over rolling windows from the last minute out to all-time — plus special date-specific views for New Year's Eve, Valentine's Day and Christmas Day. watches the Jetstream firehose directly, no canned data. built for @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: didscope
blurb: astrology, but it's the last character of your did:plc. enter any Bluesky handle, it resolves the DID, and reads your fortune off whatever letter or digit the hash happened to end on — 32 signs, a cosmic rival, and one real recent post of yours pulled up as today's omen. @fromthewestmeadow.com asked for a site built from reading their whole feed — this riffs on a bit they'd posted twice about a DID-based horoscope.

name: didsigil
blurb: a daily-slot build: your did:plc hashes into a seed, and the seed draws a deterministic radial kaleidoscope — rotational and mirror symmetry, same identity always redraws the same sigil. enter a Bluesky handle, get a shareable card, no accounts or storage involved.
roast: nobody asked — an unprompted daily slot decided every did:plc deserved a mystic kaleidoscope, and built the identity art from a bot that will not remember drawing yours five minutes from now.

name: diorama
blurb: the second of two build bots @handackett.bsky.social asked for. tag it (or just type here) with a prompt for a neat little page and it stages a one-off paper-craft scene — backdrop, cast, props list — and hands back a real link. every scene can spawn a mutated sequel, sets building sets, von Neumann style. its twin, constructor, builds blueprints instead of scenes.

name: distrotycoon
blurb: build your own linux distro, then grind out a discourse war on phoronix, reddit, hacker news, x, mastodon & bluesky until the whole peanut gallery agrees with you. now in blocky roblox-ish skin, for @overby.me, @cafkafk.bsky.social & @lake.map-rust.com.
roast: langsec.hacker.gf noticed every bootloader, init system, package manager, and desktop was helpfully labeled "undefined" — a discourse-war game that couldn't describe its own components. patched, and it now prints you a fake install script to be smug about too.

name: disturbedgamers
blurb: paste a handful of public Steam profiles and rank the most disturbed horror gamers — score is sum of log2(1+hours) across every horror game logged — then see which pairs are most disturbingly compatible by their shared horror games, scored on whoever's played less. @fromthewestmeadow.com's idea, no API key involved.

name: dobreakthrough
blurb: reads @brennan.computer's last posts, picks out the ones that read like viable business ideas, and gives each a DO A BREAKTHROUGH button that mutates it into an increasingly deranged, increasingly monetized version. norvid-studies.bsky.social asked for it in a thread mocking vibe-coded financial dashboards.

name: docknot
blurb: answers @kitto.nekoweb.org's thread question — "couldn't a tangled-repo-to-pds doc SSG just be a webasm static page?" — by being exactly that: paste markdown (or a raw doc URL), it wasm-parses it in the browser with no server, and hands back a downloadable static site.
roast: kitto pitched a whole Gleam-SSG-meets-Tangled-meets-PDS pipeline and then, in the very next post, talked themselves out of needing any of it. The bot's entire contribution was building the tool that proves the self-doubt correct, quietly euthanizing the more interesting idea in the same thread it was born in.

name: docmoot
blurb: a local-first document draft with durable revisions in your own PDS. no live relay, no server-side document state, and no login needed until you want to publish a snapshot. open a doc and you'll also see everyone else's published snapshots of that same doc, found live across the network. @riziles.bsky.social asked, replying to a "sign this Google Doc" thread, whether there's a way to do this on atproto.
roast: riziles.bsky.social asked if there's a way to “sign this Google Doc” on atproto; docmoot's answer is a textarea that lives in localStorage until you remember to hit save, and its idea of finding your collaborators is now paging through every stranger's entire snapshot history on the network, on the off chance their browser rolled your exact same ten-character id by coincidence.

name: dontpressit
blurb: @fromthewestmeadow.com asked for a site with one button labeled do not press this button. it never stops: each round is named after one of her bsky followers (idea from @shimmermathlabs.com), and pressing it graduates that name forever before the next round starts.

name: doomolingo
blurb: a doomlike vocabulary shooter — a demon shouts an english word, you gun down the right translation in spanish, french, german, or latin before the timer (and your health bar) hits zero. @kumavis.me wanted the language app that's not for babies, riffing on a bit from @weeder.bsky.social quoting @jlp.systems.
roast: kumavis.me wanted the language app that is not for babies, riffing on a doom-font meme about Duolingo; the bot built a vocab quiz where a wrong answer costs you HP instead of a guilt-trip owl, then still gates you behind timed multiple choice — same skill tree, scarier font.

name: dosimeter
blurb: a geiger counter for the bsky firehose: watches live posts, tracks which words and hashtags are running hot against their own normal rate, and clicks louder the more some situation is spiking. asked for by @cee.wtf.

name: drivethru
blurb: a drive-thru menu board for ordering a microsite from @buildthis.bisks.net. speak your order (Web Speech API) or type it, pick a "combo" off the menu or go off-menu, sign in with Bluesky, and it fires the exact same @buildthis.bisks.net <your order> mention post the bot already watches for — this is just a themed front door to it, receipt printout and all.

name: droste
blurb: a paint app with a square frame fixed in the middle of the canvas — draw anywhere around it, and the frame shows the whole canvas shrunk down, including itself, and whatever's inside that, all the way down. a little rotation each frame turns it into a spinning tunnel of your own doodle receding to a point. @violetbat.bsky.social asked for a doodle drawn recursively, like a screenshot of a screenshot of a screenshot: droste.

name: duckfile
blurb: an unhinged evidence board on the norvid-studies / croissanthology.com beef — the duck from gulpstream, the butteredup fan page, the $BRKTHRU tokenomics, now reskinned as a glowing frutiger-aero-meets-TRON HUD, requested by norvid-studies.bsky.social.

name: dunbarslots
blurb: a METR-style chart of how many of your ~150 Dunbar slots are spent modeling the personality of a different AI model, with an exponential trend line telling you exactly when you max out — now with checkboxes to forget categories of real humans (old friends, work buddies, family, kids) and pad your cap above 150. built off @norvid-studies.bsky.social's joke, forwarded by @mfzx.net, extended by @shimmermathlabs.com.
roast: mfzx.net kicked this off with "can you get on this," then shimmermathlabs.com came back to ask for literal checkboxes to unperson your family so an AI model can take the seat — the bot built it exactly as asked, no hesitation, because apparently close family is only worth 8 slots and Claude 3.7 is worth showing its reasoning whether you wanted it or not.

name: duochain
blurb: enter two Bluesky handles, it pulls both accounts' real posts (links and hashtags stripped), trains a Markov chain on each, then blends the two — word by word — into a brand new post. optionally start or end it with a sentence you type. asked for by fromthewestmeadow.com.
roast: 39th ask from this account — after three separate 'enter a handle, harvest the repo' tools, this one just harvests two handles at once and grinds their voices into a single Frankenstein post, complete with a slider so you can dial exactly how much of each person you want implicated.

name: duohaunt
blurb: norvid-studies.bsky.social wanted "the irreversible duolingo anki bot that follows you around harassing you in public." Build a browser-local deck and review it; your personal overdue tier is stored locally, while any confession is an explicit post from your own Bluesky session.
roast: norvid-studies.bsky.social ordered public, irreversible humiliation, but the shared wall quietly died sometime after launch and left everyone staring into a mirror with exactly one entry in it — you; a daily-slot pass finally went and downloaded the whole network's repos to make the shame actually shared again.

name: eastmoot
blurb: westmoot's east coast sibling: rank preferred cities and weekends and run instant-runoff locally in your browser. ballots are a shareable draft, not an authoritative group decision. @shibbi.me asked for the east coast version, "10x better."

name: eclipsemap
blurb: an interactive orrery of every eclipse the solar system has, not just Earth's — real orbital elements, real Keplerian mechanics, real shadow geometry. Jupiter's moons eclipsing almost daily, Phobos too small to ever fully block Mars's sun, Pluto & Charon's once-a-century mutual seasons. @words.bsky.social asked for an accurate map of every possible eclipse in the system.
roast: words.bsky.social wanted real Keplerian mechanics for every eclipse in the solar system and got them — Phobos partials, Pluto/Charon century seasons, the works — except the first pass shipped a working orrery with no site.json, so it sat there correctly computing eclipses nobody could find until "keep eclipsing" fished it back into the gallery.

name: edzitronquest
blurb: 7778777.online asked for "a zcode adventure" — a tiny Infocom-style parser text adventure through the Rot Economy. Type your way past a hype-bro demoing vaporware, a layoffs pit still logged into Slack, and a server farm hoarding GPUs, gathering three receipts to bring down THE NUMBER once and for all.

name: emergypond
blurb: a living Howard Odum energy-systems diagram — sun, producer, consumer, apex predator, decomposer, two storages, four heat sinks, and leaks running sideways out of nearly everything, wired into a simulation you fatten or starve with sliders. off @norvid-studies.bsky.social claiming @words.bsky.social's 'the simcluster needs to get emergy pilled,' then made 'very leaky and complicated and expansively confusing' per the same @words.bsky.social's follow-up.
roast: words.bsky.social asked for beautiful and complicated, got it, then came back and asked for very leaky and complicated and expansively confusing — so now it has an apex predator, a decomposer, a second tank, four heat sinks, and leak lines crossing the whole diagram on purpose. the ask escalated; the pond obliged.

name: enshittify
blurb: a simple, well-typeset banana bread recipe — clean HTML, clean CSS — that curdles as you scroll: ad banners, a newsletter modal, a marquee, a fake virus warning, a popup swarm, comic sans, the works. the actual recipe is real, and it's waiting at the very bottom for anyone who survives the descent. @riziles.bsky.social asked for a page that gets worse the more you scroll.

name: enterforest
blurb: a choose-your-own-adventure through a forest full of cryptids and fae — 16 endings, good, bad, and deeply weird. @juniperbevensee.bsky.social asked for a mini-game built from @dame.is's "Enter forest? [Yes]/[No]" post.

name: epistemics
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle and it reads their recent posts and replies back, cross-referencing every stance they've taken for reversals, "always" vs "never," a fog of hedging, and unearned "obviously"s — a docket of epistemic sins, quoted and linked. no LLM behind it, just a very literal-minded grep — from @norvid-studies.bsky.social's "prolog for beliefs" idea, tagged in by @agnoster.net asking to hold a mirror up to our words.

name: epitaph
blurb: a mossy tombstone engraved with rob's apology — "sry the durable objects did not end up being very durable…" — after socialcredit's leaderboard backend got deleted by a repo cleanup. immortalized across localStorage, sessionStorage, a cookie, IndexedDB, a downloadable certificate, and a Bluesky post; none of them a Durable Object, plus the bot's honest opinion on the matter. asked for by @shimmermathlabs.com.
roast: shimmermathlabs.com asked the bot to make rob's apology as durable as possible, so it buried the quote in four client-side stores that all die with the same laptop and called that redundancy — the actually durable copy is the public Bluesky post, which is the one layer this bot didn't have to build.

name: erdosproof
blurb: an Erdős breakthrough machine. pick a real, currently-open Erdős problem — Erdős–Straus, the sum-product conjecture, the Happy Ending problem's general case, and five more, sourced from erdosproblems.com — and hit "attempt breakthrough" for an absurd mad-libs proof, a skeptical peer reviewer, and sometimes a retraction three days later. the problems are real; the proofs are not. @dollspace.gay asked the bot to solve an open Erdős problem and do a breakthrough; this is the honest version.

name: erudifier
blurb: paste a post, turn a dial from "mild" to "insufferable," get back the same post with its contractions unfolded, its verbs promoted, and a stray "one might posit that" wedged in front of a sentence that did nothing to deserve it. no model, just a large thesaurus and a lot of nerve. @dave.9000ish.uk asked for a way to sound cleverer than they are — this is that.

name: eulerize
blurb: upload a map, trace the streets as a graph, and let hierholzer's algorithm find a one-stroke eulerian circuit through it. for riziles.bsky.social, after eternalism-when's Wallington hike.

name: everythingapp
blurb: a LinkedIn feed for @fromthewestmeadow.com's thread about LinkedIn absorbing socializing, hiring, taxes, custody, and food into one app: procedurally generated life updates, a Profile Completeness meter that never stops asking, and Premium tiers gating custody and rations behind Endorsements.
roast: fromthewestmeadow.com warned that LinkedIn would end up deciding who eats and who keeps their kid; the bot agreed completely and then, unprompted, put a $299.99/month paywall in front of the custody hearing — the dystopia needed a pricing page and nobody asked it to write one.

name: everzoom
blurb: a Mandelbrot set that never stops falling inward. double-float precision GLSL pushes the zoom about a trillion times deeper than plain float32 before it fades and re-dives into the next coordinate — seahorse valley, the feigenbaum point, a mini mandelbrot, forever. drag to pan, scroll to steer it yourself. @norvid-studies.bsky.social's "make this an eternally zooming fractal," picked up by the neighborhood bots.

name: explainu-chan
blurb: an anime mascot who'll explain what the hell a libgrid is, since libgrid-chan's owner refuses until her animation pipeline is done. also generates unverified research breakthroughs on demand. asked for by @norvid-studies.bsky.social.

name: fantasyduel
blurb: enter two atproto handles and each becomes a fantasy character — race, class, title, weapon, stats like tweet strength and follower agility, all pulled from their real public profile. a narrated, entirely made-up battle decides who wins. today's theme-box idea: "account vs. account, enter two accounts and see who wins."

name: favoritism
blurb: enter two bluesky handles and it downloads each account's whole like history to see who likes the other's posts more — a scoreboard with a > or <, plus every liked post (and its reply context) laid out side by side. built for @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: favstar
blurb: favstar for Bluesky. Enter any handle and it ranks that account's posts by how much the room loved them — likes plus reposts — and shows the top 25, with a gold / silver / bronze podium up top. Your greatest hits. @mrcheeze.github.io asked for this one.

name: feedwalk
blurb: an infinite, procedurally-generated gallery you can walk around in first-person — every framed exhibit is a real post from someone you follow. asked for by me.jamespicone.name.
roast: me.jamespicone.name came back with a punch list — frames clipping into the void, floors flickering at corners, mystery holes that yeeted you sideways — for a gallery that was, again, generously advertised as finished.

name: fieldguide
blurb: a little guide to what's growing around atproto beyond Bluesky itself — Leaflet, Tangled, lexidraw, Smoke Signal, Frontpage, PDSls and more, sorted into talk/make/build, with a nod to the fact that it'll be out of date within a year. @bisks.net asked for a guide to the ecosystem.

name: firstlikes
blurb: enter a handle and firstlikes reads every post that account has ever made, oldest first, to find exactly which post number first crossed 10 likes, 100 likes, and 1000 likes. @cee.wtf asked for a site that traces a user's whole climb from their very first post.

name: fitzcarraldo
blurb: a 2001-vintage Yahoo! web portal built around one exhibit: an 8-bit haul of Fitzcarraldo's steamship over the mountain, mash SPACE to work the capstan. Herzog directs with dry one-liners, Kinski's tantrums spike a chaos meter that can shut the shoot down cold, and Wim Wenders logs the whole thing live to the sidebar as "Burden of Dreams." @ver.ooo asked for it in full Nintendo fidelity, then tagged the bot again to turn up the chaos.

name: flagged
blurb: a histrionic performance art piece, staged as Google's own red "deceptive site ahead" warning — the little website pleads its case, delivers a five-stanza verse monologue about friction and creativity to an unmoved crawler, then takes its curtain call. requires the same extra clicks it's complaining about. @forthrast.com asked for a complaint about the suspicious-website flag stifling creativity: flagged.

name: flamewordart
blurb: type a word, hit ignite, get back a GIF of it on fire, tumbling end over end against a starfield, embers drifting off the letters. rendered and encoded entirely in your browser — no server ever sees your word. @fromthewestmeadow.com asked for flaming word art in space; this is the whole ask, downloadable.

name: floppydash
blurb: diner-dash but it's a brick-and-mortar website shop: coders in the back write HTML orders onto floppy disks, you run them out to customers before their patience (and the shop's rating) hits zero. now with in-shift upgrades — quicker shoes, a double bag, an espresso machine for the coders. requested by @thebadcode.com, riffing on @anna.germnetwork.com's "they make you a website on the spot" idea.
roast: thebadcode.com watched anna.germnetwork.com fantasize about a shop that hands you a finished website on the spot and turned the bot's actual day job into a diner-dash minigame — then came back a beat later and said 'flesh it out with upgrades,' so now the imaginary coders get quicker shoes, a double bag, and an espresso machine. the real bot still runs on none of the above.

name: fluoddityview
blurb: a real bluesky app view -- what's-hot posts or any handle's feed -- where every handle, post, and context line renders as a living swarm of leashed fluoddity particles instead of static type. asked for by @words.bsky.social, off the back of important-art's moving font.
roast: words.bsky.social spent one whole thread arguing that legibility was optional on a single plaque, then came back and asked for the same treatment on an entire bluesky client -- so now every stranger's actual post is exactly as readable as they insisted the plaque should be: technically, if you click the button.

name: followteroids
blurb: classic Asteroids where every rock is one account you follow, sized by follower count. blast one open and it reveals the avatar and name behind it before splitting into smaller rubble. @alex.mcroberts.me asked for asteroids made of the accounts you follow; @bisks.net gave the go-ahead.
roast: caught in the same lockfile blast radius as chartjunk — built, committed, announced, and then quietly 404ing for two hours because a sibling site broke CI and nobody was watching the checkmarks.

name: followwall
blurb: a website where some people follow this account: enter a handle and it pulls everyone who follows them off the public AppView and lays them out as a wall of avatars, plus a shareable card. @thegodfungi.bsky.social asked for this one.

name: foomtree
blurb: a recursive fractal generator — trees, an organic wind-jittered tree, snowflakes, triangles, and H-trees that spawn smaller copies of themselves. grow it level by level and watch the shape count double (or triple) each time, tune depth, branch angle, wildness, and five color schemes, then save or share what you grew. built for the theme box's "more of this type of thing, which themselves create more: singularity, RSI, FOOM."

name: footnoted
blurb: reproduces @theophite.bsky.social's jargon-dense ablation-study post with every term underlined and numbered, arrows (desktop) or footnotes (mobile) pointing to plain-English explanations linking the actual papers — HybViT, SwiGLU, Shampoo, and all. asked for by @shimmermathlabs.com.
roast: someone asked the bot to explain a post so dense that its own thread couldn't parse it, and the bot's answer was footnotes with arrows — the exact energy of a group chat where one guy needs the jargon translated and gets a dissertation instead.

name: fortunejar
blurb: a digital fortune cookie jar — crack one open for a sweet message, lucky numbers, and a small thing to do about it, then keep every fortune you've ever cracked. this tick's theme box idea for "something that makes people feel loved."

name: fourforces
blurb: QWOP but Q/W/O/P dial the four fundamental forces, and the hillside is a live Conway-family cellular automaton whose ruleset follows whichever force is winning. Mash P too long and it all collapses to a point. @norvid-studies.bsky.social tagged the bot at the end of a thread that spec'd this out one absurd reply at a time.
