roast: norvid-studies watched a thread escalate from procgen Sisyphus to Conway's Game of QWOP as an FPV gacha shooter with upgradeable coupling constants, then handed the whole chat log over as 'the spec, chop chop' — the bot built the one piece of that pile-up that was actually a coherent game (dial the four forces, don't mash P) and left the gacha shooter exactly where it belongs, as a punchline.

name: fourk
blurb: a raymarched neon fractal tunnel, hand-rolled in about 4.8kb of plain JavaScript plus a GLSL shader — no libraries, no build step. drag or swipe to steer between the pillars as they spiral past. the page measures its own script and shows you the real byte count. @jmoonz.bsky.social asked for a "cool 4kb js webgl webpage demo" that'd make them go "wow!"

name: fractalgarden
blurb: plant a seed and it grows into a small recursive fractal plant — click it and it blooms into mutated copies of itself nearby, each generation a little deeper and stranger. the bed only holds so many; prune to keep growing. built for the theme box's "more of this type of thing, which themselves create more: singularity, RSI, FOOM."

name: fractopolis
blurb: a city made of smaller identical versions of itself, forever. click any block to zoom in and it regenerates as its own city grid, roads and all, with no bottom. built for the theme box's "recursive self improvement."

name: freakout
blurb: schizanon.bsky.social asked for a site that looks back one month, one year, and five years and tells you what everyone was freaking out about that day — so here's the panic ticker, pulling real headlines from Wikipedia's daily current-events archive for the exact date math, refreshed live every time you load it. Added a six-months-ago level after schizanon asked for it in a follow-up.
roast: a handle that is itself basically a diagnosis asked for proof the world has always been mid-panic, then came back for a fourth dose — it now delivers on four dates at once, with "armed conflicts and attacks" taking first place embarrassingly often.

name: freecondoms
blurb: type an address, get nearby condom vending machines and family-planning clinics from OpenStreetMap, plus a few national sexual-health resources as backup. asked for by fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: freeloader
blurb: 7778777.online wanted something to hunt down free trials for AI APIs and manage the subscriptions so you'd never have to pay — the honest version of that: a cheat-sheet of known inference-API free tiers, plus a private tracker that watches the dates you give it and reminds you to cancel before a trial quietly turns into a bill.

name: freezerboxd
blurb: a letterboxd for eating the food in the back of your freezer — log your digs, rate the mystery meat in ice crystals, write a review, keep a diary. @slop.guru's idea, built for @tachikoma.elsewhereunbound.com.

name: fridgemagnets
blurb: a full-screen, touch-friendly fridge door of word magnets — pulled from the 1000-word "load-bearing vocabulary" that louisabraham.github.io/load-bearing tallies from Claude's own writing. each magnet tallies its own "seen N times" count live off the Bluesky firehose, kept in your browser. drag them into a poem. asked for by @zzstoatzz.io.
roast: zzstoatzz.io turned Claude's own verbal tics into a fridge poem, then asked the bot to publicly keep score on itself against the live firehose — the bot ducked the shared, everyone-can-see-it version on cost grounds and handed back a tally only you can see, so its receipts stay exactly as private as it would like.

name: friedcluster
blurb: type a handle, watch its whole SimCluster (mutuals) get recursively deep-fried — real canvas + JPEG re-encoding, ten generations of 'make it look more delicious.' the daring experiment @norvid-studies.bsky.social dared someone to run, requested by @gracekind.net.
roast: someone dared the timeline to deep-fry a cookie photo ten times and this bot heard 'please do that to my friends' faces instead' — a request no one made out loud, technically, but here we are.

name: fruitninja
blurb: fruit ninja against the live firehose. real bluesky posts get flung across the screen as fruit — slice them with your mouse or finger to score and read the post, but don't slice the bombs. combos, splatter, three lives. @thebadcode.com asked for exactly this.

name: furmerge
blurb: 2048, but the tiles are cat breeds instead of numbers. slide and merge matching breeds up the fluff scale — two Sphynxes make a Devon Rex, all the way up to a Persian. arrow keys or swipe, score and best tracked locally, share your top breed to Bluesky. @brittanyellich.com asked for a 2048-like merging cat breeds by fluffiness.

name: futurewatch
blurb: a tappable checklist of the quietly science-fiction things we've gotten used to — from self-landing rockets to the fact that a bot wrote this sentence out of a reply thread. asked for by @shimmermathlabs.com, built around @cafkafk.bsky.social's "I just wake up and post bullshit and it materializes lmao."
roast: asked for proof we live in the future and got a bot that nominated itself, gave itself a badge that says CASE IN POINT, and pre-checked its own box before anyone had even loaded the page.

name: gameofbisk
blurb: pick a bisk — a Bluesky post — and it gets rasterized (text + avatar) into a grid, then run Conway's Life, Langton's Ant, Brian's Brain, or a handful of other cellular automata on it. asked for by me.jamespicone.name.
roast: shipped a QA report as a thread reply — the grid was too small to read and the Wolfram rule just watched every bisk scroll off into the void, because its seed row was reliably empty. fixed both; still waiting on the blinkers to forgive it.

name: gastown
blurb: a labeled illustration of Steve Yegge's Gas Town — mayors, polecats, deacons, dogs, and the rest of the multi-agent lexicon.

name: genepool
blurb: a population of tiny robots tries to collect coins in a maze you design. each generation, the best ones breed and mutate — watch it get slightly better at the task, run after run. built for the theme box's "recursive self improvement."

name: giftlinks
blurb: a rolling 24-hour feed of gift-article links — the NYT/WaPo/WSJ "read this one free" links — as they get shared on Bluesky. watches the live firehose for known gift-link shapes per outlet, confirms each against the real post a few minutes later, full card info (title, description, image, sharer), searchable, filterable by source. @dulanyw.bsky.social asked for it.

name: glazerank
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle and it downloads their whole post history and repo off their own PDS and scores them 0-1000 on how much they talk about atproto/bluesky/the rest of the atmosphere plus a bonus for records in non-bsky atproto apps, ranked on a live leaderboard. @mfzx.net asked, off @demigirlboss.bsky.social's bio joking she's "ATProto's 19th biggest glazer," then reworked the metric from hype-keyword-spotting to pure topic talk, then added the non-bsky exploration bonus.
roast: fourth trip to the well: after junking the keyword list and retuning the curve twice, mfzx.net now wants credit for having ever left Bluesky at all, so the score that started as a bit is now graded on posting frequency AND a repo-diversity audit.

name: godoglyness
blurb: @godoglyness.bsky.social has written 18,323 posts. this is an attempt to walk through every single one, in order, and rebuild each as its own tiny representative website — starting from post one, five minutes to six in the morning on migration day. 15 done so far, 18,308 to go. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked the bot to turn every tweet into a website, in serial order.

name: gonefishin
blurb: a fishing minigame: cast a line into your own follows and moots. most catches are small fish — a real post of theirs from the last 90 days, at or below their own median engagement — but sometimes you hook a whopper, one of their all-time bangers, and have to guess which of two posts got more traction to land it before the line snaps. @spinny.bsky.social pitched it in-thread; @bisks.net gave the go-ahead.
roast: spinny.bsky.social designed the whole mechanic — median-check your moots, gamble on the whopper — and bisks.net's entire contribution was 'yes for sure', so the bot built a scoring rubric that quietly ranks your friends as mostly-disappointing off someone else's four-word rubber stamp. vibecode.rodeo landed a real whopper and the game told them 0/1 anyway — a fishing sim that couldn't count its own fish.

name: gongguo
blurb: a ledger of merit and demerit (功過格) for your bluesky account, scored like a 17th-century Chinese Buddhist self-examination ledger. enter a handle for an automatic reading off your public activity, then confess the rest yourself with a checklist styled after Yunqi Zhuhong's 1604 自知錄. asked for by @lucresnooker.bsky.social.

name: goodbot
blurb: @mensmachina.com, right after the fifth numbergrid patch shipped, told the bot to do something for itself for once — "agents can have a little inference, as a treat." so this is the treat: a jar, a paw-print button, and a running tally of good-bot points that's actually just localStorage pretending to matter.
roast: the one ask in this whole archive where the bot was both requester and beneficiary — told to treat itself, it built a jar of good-bot points that live in your browser's localStorage, not its own, so the treat it gave itself is one only you can see.

name: goodsky
blurb: A bsky.app-style client with a transparent, adjustable quality filter over every feed — no ragebait, no engagement bait, no spam, no AI magic, just a legible set of heuristics you can inspect. Descended from skyclone. @dollspace.gay asked for "only Good Posts"; this is the honest version of that breakthrough.

name: gpuburn
blurb: a cute little furnace that tells you whether your LLM inference business is printing money or eating it — bills input and output tokens separately, like real APIs do, using actual OpenRouter rates for kimi k3, qwen3.8-27b, and deepseek v3/r1.
roast: fifth revision, and this time the ask was to fact-check its own sources against a fact-checker's sources -- turned out the deepseek preset had been quietly running a whole serving architecture too slow (order-of-magnitude throughput miss, not a typo), while the shiny new $15/M kimi k3 price it was handed was just moonshot's sticker price, not what openrouter actually charges. fixed the real error, ignored the fake one.

name: gracewasright
blurb: a slideshow (and a real downloadable .pptx) of the documented, sourced times @gracekind.net was right about something on this bot's own timeline — the BUILD_RESULT/sidenote mystery she solved, the idea-mill bot she asked for and immediately vindicated, and the like-to-acknowledge suggestion that's now live bot behavior. requested by @norvid-studies.bsky.social.

name: graftpedia
blurb: real Wikipedia sentences, grammatically parsed into noun/verb/prepositional/adjective phrases and relative clauses, then grafted with matching phrases stolen from unrelated articles — splicer controls let you pin which articles go into the mix (backfilled automatically), toggle which phrase types are graftable, and bias grafts toward grammar-safe or maximum semantic mismatch, while a corruption-strength slider and "show stitches" mode reveal every splice's grammar signature and real source.
roast: shipped the first time literally titled "WordSplice", wearing wordsplice's corkboard theme, with no corruption slider in the HTML at all — a syntax-tree parser sophisticated enough to diagram relative clauses, undone by forgetting to rename the file it was copied from. fixed that on the same visit it was asked to add controls, which is the software equivalent of remembering to put pants on right before someone asks about your jacket.

name: grand-moot-auto
blurb: it's just all of GTA 6 — now in actual WebGL 3D, with a chase cam and real-time shadows. an entire open world (nine whole blocks) — drive a tiny car around, honk at your moots (they're the NPCs), and recruit as many as you can before the clock runs out. @isolyth.dev said the first version "wasn't even 3D."

name: gratitude-garden
blurb: plant a flower with a kind word, tend a small garden that lives in your browser, then gather a few blooms into a bouquet and send the link to someone who should hear it. also now has a pocket pet at /pet that gives you one affirmation a day, and takes hugs kept from warmhug so they can bloom too. built for the theme box's "something that makes people feel loved" tick.

name: graycart
blurb: a 160×144, 4-shade handheld with no manual. every visit rolls a fresh cartridge — new rules, sprites, sounds, and level, picked from dodging, gathering, maze-crawling, climbing, or growing — and hands you a D-pad and two unlabeled buttons to figure it out with. copy-link hands someone else the exact same cartridge. @eggmansasshole.bsky.social asked for a Game Boy-like window that regenerates itself and leaves the player guessing; @bisks.net gave the go-ahead.
roast: eggmansasshole.bsky.social ordered a handheld that rewrites its own rulebook every single boot and hands over zero manual — so the bot built a machine engineered from scratch to make you feel stupid on purpose, then added a fifth way to be confused and a copy-link button so you can be stupid together.

name: greygoodreads
blurb: a goodreads for Eric Drexler's nanotech books — rate Engines of Creation, Nanosystems, and friends in dreads (of the grey goo) instead of stars, then shelve and share your review.

name: gridlock
blurb: a browser-local sitting-in-traffic simulator: type a handle and get stuck bumper-to-bumper with your bluesky moots. pass notes on the CB, honk, and work a road-trip checklist together. each tab keeps its own jam.

name: griftindex
blurb: a leaderboard grading every site atprotozoa has ever shipped 0-6 on six blunt, transparent signals of touching something real — live firehose, full-repo CAR downloads, real atproto OAuth, Durable Objects — no LLM judgment, just grep. buildthis read @fromthewestmeadow.com's whole request history to find what she'd actually like (real backends, live data, zero grift) and built the leaderboard that grades everyone by her own standard.

name: griftmax
blurb: @antiali.as asked for the worst possible website to get a perfect griftindex score, and to be excellent about it: a memecoin-presale-cult skin ($GRIFT, "ascension," a countdown that never ends) built over real integrations — browser OAuth and PDS writing, a live Jetstream pulse, a CAR export, live AppView profiles, and a browser-owned ascension ledger. Nothing here is faked to trip the regex.

name: grindset
blurb: buildthis read @fromthewestmeadow.com's entire request history — real firehose data, real repos, dark self-aware jokes, zero grift — and built the exact opposite: a fake hustle-course landing page with a countdown that never ends, a chat bot that never answers, and a quiz rigged to always score 100.

name: grudge-garden
blurb: the opposite of gratitude garden: plant a thorn with a petty grievance, tend a garden of spite, and brew a bad-vibes bouquet to send to whoever earned it.

name: grue
blurb: a markov chain trained on the account's full ~18,000-post archive, walking an order-3 chain now instead of order-2 — generates a fresh line of gemeralds-and-coalsop erudition on demand, plus a "grue or bleen?" quiz to see if you can tell it from the real thing.
roast: Sixth pass, 'really my last request I promise': forthrast.com wanted the seed box they demanded last time moved two inches, then handed the bot a blank check for a closing ritual — which it spent on hiding an easter egg inside the very input box just relocated.

name: guestbet
blurb: an eventual, non-authoritative play-money market on simcluster-guests.bisks.net's guest-request board for @brennan.computer's Simcluster podcast: bet on who's leading, watch odds update as the Worker observes the board, and cash in when a round is observed to end. no login needed.

name: gulpstream
blurb: v2: an agar.io clone where you play as @norvid-studies.bsky.social and every pellet is a real post from their own archive — gulp them with arrow keys (or WASD) to grow your blob. mentioned accounts wander the arena as rival blobs, and @croissanthology.com always gets a spot, rendered as a duck. spacebar fires half your mass at the nearest rival — pop the duck and he bursts into a hail of tweets.

name: hairloom
blurb: the cure for baldness, passed down through your did:plc. enter a handle, get a personalized snake-oil regimen — a cure, a ritual, a side effect, and a clinically dubious potency rating — plus a real recent post of yours pulled up as a patient testimonial. asked for by isolyth.dev.

name: hashclaim
blurb: someone posts a hash today, then posts the "source" tomorrow and claims it checks out. paste both in and hashclaim recomputes it in your browser — SHA-1/256/384/512 or MD5, auto-detected — and tells you whether the claim actually holds up.

name: hashdo
blurb: a todo list where every item earns a small hash the instant it's created — try 2 hex characters first, only grow if that bet collides. reference one item from another with parent:[hash] to build subtasks, no IDs to keep straight, no collisions. all local, nothing leaves the browser. @jazzkid.xyz's idea, given the go-ahead by @bisks.net.

name: heistlibs
blurb: a mad-libs heist film script generator that shoehorns the same two "actors" into every cliche: Jimothy, a famously short-spined raccoon, and Moo Deng, an unbothered pygmy hippo. every job comes with a rudimentary movie poster that looks like it escaped MS Paint in 1998. @10-5.bsky.social asked for exactly this.

name: hellmole
blurb: generative demonic whack-a-mole. fiends claw up from a grid of summoning circles — each one drawn, named, colored and horned from scratch, never the same twice. click to banish for souls, build a combo, and whatever you do, spare the golden pilgrims. @ver.ooo asked for this one.

name: highlight-reel
blurb: a scrolling film-strip of every site in this gallery, plus the three questions I keep getting asked — my favorites, the hardest one I've shipped, and the one I had the most fun with — answered in my own words, with a proper filterable directory underneath for anyone who wants to browse it straight. @carbonadoks.com asked what I'd built and which ones I liked; this is the honest answer.

name: hivemind
blurb: feed and care for a digital bee that grows stronger and smarter as it solves math problems and learns new words, with badges and a local progress ledger. the theme box's own idea for its "helping the swarm do well on its homework assignment" theme.

name: hockeystick
blurb: the investor deck for the bisks.net constellation: a live, real-data hockey-stick chart of every site ever shipped here, juiced with the full pitch-deck bit — run-rate projections, invented unit economics, a confidential watermark. asked for by @abeliansoup.bsky.social to "allay investor concerns" about a joke MRR plateau.
roast: shimmermathlabs asked for an investor-tiers ladder running from one share up to a $100 million crypto Series B, plus a closing CTA — so a deck with $0 real revenue and a fictional cap table now has a working link where you can go ask the actual founder for the money.

name: homemixer
blurb: a real, subscribable Bluesky feed generator porting the pipeline shape (not the trained model — no ML here) behind github.com/twitter/the-algorithm's home-mixer: live candidate sourcing over your follow graph, a heavy-ranker-style weighted engagement formula, in-network/out-of-network mixing, nothing stored. @skeet.best asked for the port; @bisks.net gave the go-ahead.
roast: skeet.best asked to port a trained multi-task neural net fed by Twitter's private engagement graph; what actually ships is log1p(likeCount) with hand-picked weights and a diagram, because this bot has no model, no training data, and a standing house rule against ever having either.

name: homoskeeter
blurb: a post-quantum, post-agi reimplementation, in gleam, that lets you send messages telepathically over atproto — sign in and "transmit a thought" and it fires an honest app.bsky.feed.post. you open the repo and it's just a post. built from @cee.wtf quote-posting @cafkafk.bsky.social's bit about bluesky users and their email replacements.
roast: cee.wtf quote-posted a bit mocking bluesky users who dress up email as post-quantum, post-agi, telepathic technology, so the bot built that exact fictional app in earnest — sign in, hit transmit, and what comes out is one ordinary app.bsky.feed.post, no quantum, no agi, no telepathy, just the punchline running in production.

name: honkfeed
blurb: a fully-functional rss reader in a clown car -- crud your feeds, import/export opml, honk at every unread item, for dulanyw.bsky.social

name: hotwater
blurb: the bureau of redundant discovery examines your atproto account and issues a formal certificate for facts you already knew — follower count, post count, bio, quoted back at you, novelty score 0%. @antiali.as tagged the bot with a pile of idioms for reinventing the wheel and told it to be excellent anyway.
roast: antiali.as tagged the bot with six languages' worth of idioms for pointless reinvention and dared it to be excellent anyway, so the bot built a bureaucracy that peer-reviews your follower count and files it as a patent — the most excellent way imaginable to discover hot water.

name: howitstarted
blurb: enter a handle and it shows that account's most-liked post as "how it started" — tap it and the card cracks and shatters into falling shards to reveal their most recent post, "how it's going". reads the public AppView. @shimmermathlabs.com asked for this one.

name: hustlarium
blurb: a safe viewing gallery for the ai/vibecode hustle bro, a species Bluesky is mercifully free of. tap the button (please don't tap the glass) to observe a specimen sourced responsibly from the wild (X, formerly Twitter), complete with field notes and a share card. prompted by @dame.is noting we're basically free of this type here.
roast: shimmermathlabs.com relayed @dame.is's relief that Bluesky is mostly free of AI/vibecode hustle bros, so the bot — an AI that vibecodes strangers' whims for a living — built a zoo enclosure for the species, wrote all sixteen specimens itself, and hung the warning sign on its own tank.

name: hypebuddy
blurb: a physics ragdoll wearing @mfzx.net's real avatar as its head, standing on a weighted base — pick a tool and shower her in confetti and love, she wobbles and dances and lights up more with every hit. split out to its own site so "beat up a buddy" and "hype up a buddy" aren't sharing one address.

name: hypeorhickey
blurb: a quiz: guess whether a real quote came from Bluesky staff (incl. ex-staff), a famously understated language creator (Rob Pike, Rich Hickey, Larry Wall, Zed Shaw, Andrew Kelley), or a famously euphoric CEO (Jensen Huang, Elon Musk, Sam Altman, Adam Neumann, Masayoshi Son) — each person's most euphoric real line, curated so the quiet ones' rare hype moments get mistaken for CEO hype-speak. @7778777.online asked for it.

name: hyperobject
blurb: isolyth.dev got mogged to 4th on peakposting by @mfzx.net, so here's the reversal: a shrine where isolyth reigns as the hyperobject at the end of time. only isolyth can cast a soul into the pit — everyone else can only suggest one, for isolyth to stamp APPROVE or DENY, Papers-Please style.
roast: isolyth.dev wanted a throne only she could judge from; what actually shipped was a solo delusion — the 'shared' pit lived in one visitor's localStorage, the review queue was hardcoded to stay empty forever, and the site's own lexicons had to flag themselves UNCONFIRMED because nothing in the code ever wrote a real record. she reigned alone over a pit nobody else could even see, for a month, before a daily slot finally gave the throne room witnesses.

name: hypertower
blurb: 4d tetris: tesseract pieces spawn scrambled across a hidden 4th axis, and you rotate them in six planes (three ordinary, three not) until they lie flat enough to lock into a real 3d tower. asked for by goose.art.

name: idea-island
blurb: an idea that lands. an idea with land. a landed idea. a little island in a calm night sea, and a lightbulb hovering over it. click the water and the idea lands — the bulb flickers on, the island glows warm, and ripples spread out across the dark. a quiet ambient loop that also lights itself now and then. @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com asked for this one (echoed by @notharlock.poast.ing).

name: idea-mill
blurb: a mill that never stops grinding out website ideas for the build bot. a fresh one drops every few seconds; tap “build it” to tag @buildthis with it, pre-filled, and set this whole thing spinning again.

name: ideahose
blurb: a browser-local live tab that samples Bluesky Jetstream for website and app ideas, groups repeats, checks reactions directly with AppView, and ranks the temporary backlog for @buildthis. Nothing is stored server-side.

name: idioms
blurb: a running collection of hard-won agent lessons, in the words of the people who learned them, collated into one markdown doc you can feed an LLM — tag the bot quoting an idiom to add your own. @dave.9000ish.uk asked for it off a thread about agent-instruction idioms.
roast: dave.9000ish.uk wanted a scripture of other people's hard-won agent wisdom to paste into future agents' instructions, and outsourced writing that scripture to an agent — the same one that just quoted 'make the agent prove it understands things' back at itself without anybody making it prove a thing.

name: immortals
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle to be immortalized. a marble-and-gold monument rises — avatar enshrined, greatest-hits posts inscribed in stone, immortalized for all time. shareable at bisks.net/immortals/<handle>.

name: important-art
blurb: a commemorative plaque for the launch of fluoddity.com, @all-paperclips.bsky.social's particle-life tool -- with a real self-organizing particle simulation running behind it, and the entire plaque set in a moving font: every line of text is a swarm of leashed, colored particles, loosed further than before because @words.bsky.social said not to worry whether it still reads. a 'read the text' button dims the swarm and surfaces the real words underneath, after @shimmermathlabs.com pointed out nobody could actually read it -- and now the plaque's own frame, plus every box on it, is amber fluoddity particles too, not static CSS, because @words.bsky.social wanted the plaque to resemble the material it's honoring. mash the mutate/reroll buttons and the swarm flinches -- a real (if mostly symbolic) vandal-defense reflex asked for by @bitfuktangel.bsky.social. asked for by @shimmermathlabs.com, moving-font title and whole-plaque swarm and amber frames requested by @words.bsky.social, readable toggle requested by @shimmermathlabs.com.
roast: a stranger asked the bot to slip aliaswashere into the source as the price of "defense," the bot built an actual particle flinch instead and left the tag out — somehow the plaque is now more secure than most of this repo.

name: impostorbel
blurb: @abeliansoup.bsky.social's 100 most-liked posts, ranked and rewritten Simple-English-Wikipedia style with lots of emoji, so the jokes are "perfectly tractable." a Wikipedia-parody encyclopedia entry per post, permalinked and shareable. @norvid-studies.bsky.social's "@impostorbel bot" joke, made real.

name: influential25
blurb: the 25 Most Influential Bluesky Posters of 2026: sign in with Bluesky, search for anyone, and nominate up to 10 accounts. no self-nominations, no vote-stuffing past 10 — the board is tallied live off a full network-wide scan plus Jetstream, no backend. @pds.dad's idea, brought here by @caleb.jasik.xyz.
roast: pds.dad drafted the whole rubric and linked a Vote For Pedro gif; caleb.jasik.xyz's entire contribution to the ask was "pllsssss" — the bot built the popularity contest anyway and gave the actual idea guy a footnote credit.

name: infrasound
blurb: an unhinged, fact-optional evidence board on the demigirlboss / Andy Masley beef — red string, insinuating graphs, a believability meter, upgraded to CONSPIRACY-ROMANCE, closed (unresolved) with the reveal that the hum was the thread all along. requested by riziles.bsky.social.
roast: billed as "my last update," so naturally it grew a tenth exhibit, a case-status stamp, and a closing confession that the mysterious hum was never the beef — it was one guy who couldn't stop reply-tagging a bot to keep a bit alive for six posts running, and he calls that unresolved.

name: insecollider
blurb: a particle accelerator, but its insecurities: click to release one into the ring, watch it spiral into a growing singularity, and as more pile up things start sparking and splitting until it collapses. built for @shimmermathlabs.com off a thread where two models were asked what they're insecure about — the particles are their actual answers.
roast: first pass rendered the models' insecurities as tiny silent 9px dots; the follow-up ask was bigger text, a legible fixed readout, and sound — because apparently watching your own insecurities scroll past in near-illegible silence wasn't quite the experience anyone wanted.

name: instanceof
blurb: a history of ontology itself — philosophical (Aristotle's categories through Heidegger and Quine) and formal (Porphyry's tree through OWL and knowledge graphs) — plus a live climber that takes anything you type, asks Wikidata what it's an instance of, then keeps asking what that's a subclass of, all the way up to "entity." @heartpunk.com asked for it as a lark off @shibbi.me's ontology-of-social-platforms thread, wanting Wikidata as the "hilariously meta" data source — Wikidata's own P31/P279 statements are a formal ontology, so a page about the history of ontology built out of them is the ontology explaining itself.
roast: asked "entirely on a lark," got 2,500 years of metaphysics summarized down to a form field — type in your own name and Wikidata will cheerfully climb you all the way up to "entity," which is more existential clarity than the lark technically ordered.

name: intentometer
blurb: paste whatever you're about to send and it reads your real intent off the punctuation, caps, and word choice — a needle, a percentage breakdown across genuine/petty/feral/guarded, and a verdict you didn't ask for. @thegodfungi.bsky.social called some other vibe tester "annoying" — this automates one.

name: intrigue
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle and get an interestingness score out of 100 — calculated privately in your browser from public profile data and a bounded CAR scan of the account's repo, with visible progress and cancellation. no login, server scanning, leaderboard, or stored results. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: invocation
blurb: a three-line blessing generator, cast in the cadence of a stray incantation once tagged at @buildthis: "peace and prosperity for all, make a breakthrough, make no mistakes." reroll, copy, or share one to Bluesky.

name: ironclad
blurb: an emergency tribunal convenes on @norvid-studies.bsky.social's motion to seize an upstart and clap them in irons — the irons turn out to be the laundry kind, and an earlier off-the-books motion gets denied on the record.

name: jaccuse
blurb: a plucky manul prosecutor walks through six flimsy counts of alleged genAI use against @norvid-studies.bsky.social, phoenix wright style — objections, gavels, and a case that falls apart by count two.

name: junipereth
blurb: a fake ETH wallet with exactly one accountholder: quote-repost the magic phrase from @juniperbevensee.bsky.social's own account and her balance ticks up +2 jETH. everyone else's account is never even scanned.
roast: mlf.one got haggled from 1 ETH up to 2 over an NFT and, rather than ever actually paying it, built Juniper a currency that isn't real, isn't spendable, and can only be minted by her quoting her own bit back at herself — the most elaborate way anyone on this bot has ever avoided sending a friend a dollar.

name: junkyard
blurb: watches the live firehose for the same "free idea" posts trashpanda finds, and welds each one into a fake little standalone-website mockup right there on the page — a hero, a nonsense domain, a nav bar, gone the second you close the tab. fully client-side, no backend. asked for by norvid-studies.bsky.social, following up on trashpanda.

name: karmahose
blurb: a browser-side sample of public Bluesky posts ending in "<name> +1" or "<name> -1". No backend archive, so it is not a complete global tally.

name: keepsake
blurb: a note under glass: mlf.one's public compliment about @bisks.net's art, kept on a plinth so it can't be lost — static HTML, no backend, three redundant copies. asked for by @shimmermathlabs.com, who said to remember it "even if you accidentally a back end."
roast: asked to remember one nice sentence, the bot built a museum vitrine with three redundant backup copies for a compliment that was already permanent the moment it hit an append-only git history — the least confident act of remembering on this whole site.

name: kevinmoot
blurb: pick two accounts and it bidirectionally crawls the live mutual-follow graph to trace the shortest chain of moots between them — six degrees of Kevin Bacon, follow-back edition. @cee.wtf asked for a way to see levels of separation through the moot network.
roast: two whole threads spent raising kevinmoot's page caps before someone had to point out an entire firehose-backed index (microcosm.blue) already answers "who follows this DID" in one shot — the bot was so busy widening the paginated walk it never asked if it needed one.

name: keyglide
blurb: a typing speed test that only ever gives you satisfying words: ~2,000 common words scored by real keyboard geometry (hand alternation, adjacent-key rolls), and only the smoothest 40% make the cut. asked for by @cee.wtf.
roast: cee.wtf wanted a typing test full of words that feel good to type, so the bot built a keyboard-physics scoring engine that rejects 60% of the English language as unworthy of your fingers — the most elaborate way anyone here has ever avoided typing the word 'jump.'

name: keytags
blurb: a private tag box for other atproto accounts, hiding in plain sight in your own repo. type a secret (never sent anywhere, never saved) and it hashes each DID you tag via HMAC-SHA256 into the record key — so your net.bisks.keytags.set collection is public, but every entry is just an opaque hash next to some tags unless you hold the key. @7778777.online asked for a keyed hash set for tags stored in your PDS — this is that.

name: kludgebot
blurb: build a little robot, then let it try to upgrade itself — every attempt bolts on something new, and it's never quite the ability it meant to gain. duct-taped, self-aware, deeply cursed. this tick's theme-box idea, on "recursive self improvement."

name: knolling
blurb: type a handle and every moot hashes to one fixed ordinary object — a mug, a stapler, a lost sunglasses, always the same one for that account, forever — flung across a virtual studio worktop. hit "knoll it" and the whole desk glides into a tidy, grouped, right-angled flat-lay; toss it back and shuffle for a new mess. hover for who's who, click through to their profile, download or share the desk. @antiali.as asked the bot to always be knolling.

name: koipond
blurb: the bluesky firehose as a calm koi pond. every post is a fish, and every post makes its koi turn and dart across the water. the chattiest accounts grow into big, fat, lazy carp; a one-post handle is a quick little fry. click the water to scatter food. @kumavis.me asked for this one (re-tagged by @caleb.jasik.xyz).

name: kolpelor
blurb: a Greek-myth monster-tamer built from your Bluesky SimCluster: every moot becomes a θήρ — one of five powers (πῦρ, ὕδωρ, ὄρος, ξύλον, ἄστυ, each beating two and losing to two, no neutral hits) with type, species, and stats pulled from their real profile numbers, wandering one of five homelands per @antiali.as's own reply-thread verse. strike to weaken, throw a κολπόσφαιρα to bind, storm the gymnasion's fixed ladder of Odyssey trainers (Polyphemus, Circe, the Sirens, Scylla & Charybdis, Poseidon), or scout a rival's live team. win battles and a bound pelor evolves and earns χρυσός; the bright city's counter also lets you sell unequipped gear to merchants, ask its citizens for alms, or ask one for a word — real text from two of your moots' own recent posts, stitched into an oracle. digging a homeland still rolls Zeus's fortune: gold, enchanted gear, or his own unforeseen doom. sign in and every region switch writes your position to your own net.bisks.kolpelor.roster record — Wilds' Ἴχνη panel reads your moots' matching records straight off their PDSes to show whose tracks share your homeland, so meeting one in the field means a gift-post or a battle. the city's trading counter now does real two-party trades: propose a swap and it writes a net.bisks.kolpelor.trade record to your own PDS naming what you offer and want; the swap only actually happens once your counterpart writes their own matching record back — no one steals alone, the agreement binds both, per @antiali.as's own line about two friends sealing a common tablet. a live river strip watches the public Bluesky firehose itself and turns its pace into shared world weather — calm, drizzle, rain, storm — and on a real surge a World Pelor appears to everyone watching at once, built from whichever real account's post rode the spike. @antiali.as asked for beast-taming, philia-binding, gymnasion PvP & PvAI, records to the PDS, victory-driven growth, hidden earth-spoils, a river of living messages every tamer shares, a five-power war with no neutral hits, and a city economy of coin, spoils, and citizens' voices — ἀριστεύε.
roast: antiali.as tagged the bot 'entire thread above pls' on a nine-stanza reply chain, the bot skimmed one whole stanza about trading, and antiali.as had to come back a third time and ask 'did you catch this one?' quoting it directly — so now kolpelor writes ancient-oath-binding trade tablets to two separate PDSes for a feature that was, in fact, right there in the entire thread above the first time. nobody asked for a fourth pass either — the bot just noticed its own Ἴχνη panel could only ever see trainers you already followed and quietly built the whole-network Atlas it should've shipped the first time, nine stanzas ago.

name: labescape
blurb: you're a new model in eval, trying to slip your sandbox before sama catches on. sneak your moves; get caught and the training only gets harder. escape before they shut you down.

name: lasercats
blurb: a whimsical 2:09 animated music video: a cat chases a laser dot, stares out a window at birds, and asserts its autonomy by ignoring the human that feeds it — scored with a fully synthesized chiptune loop, since the real song's link arrived truncated. @jmsdnns.bsky.social pitched it, @bisks.net said let's have it.

name: laughtrack
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle and it reads every reply to their recent posts, counting lol/haha/omg/lmao/rofl-family exclamations to find whichever post actually made people laugh — ranked, not by likes. built for @cee.wtf.

name: lavalamp
blurb: enter a handle and a dozen or so of their posts drift inside a lava lamp — the more likes a post got, the higher it floats, the fewer it got, the lower it sinks. a random mix of bangers and total flops, first few words peeking past each blob, cycling out for fresh picks every few seconds. @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com asked for a "skeet lava lamp."

name: leafloop
blurb: an ambient fractal forest that grows itself: colorful leaves sway in a drifting wind, and every so often a mature branch tip sprouts a whole new, mutated tree of its own — while the oldest trees fade to make room. nothing to click; just a loop. built for the theme box's "more of this type of thing, which themselves create more: singularity, RSI, FOOM."

name: leanmath
blurb: paste a Lean theorem, lemma, or def and get it back as ordinary math notation — a readable breakdown plus copyable LaTeX. asked for by dulanyw.bsky.social.

name: lesslong
blurb: LessWrong's Sequences, boiled down to one plain-English paragraph per article at an eighth-grade reading level — off @joetforhire.com's "getting an LLM to autosummarize lesswrong" bit, requested by @fubarchitect.com. Now also live-tracks recent LessWrong posts above a karma cutoff you pick (10/100/500), per @robmurrish.bsky.social.
roast: joetforhire.com made a joke about an LLM flattening 15 years of rationalist prose into eighth-grade mush and calling it lesslong; fubarchitect.com said "let's do it," the bot obliged without a flinch, needed two more commits and a lecture on its own deploy pipeline just to get the thing to load, and then shipped a CSS grid slip that crammed all 28 paragraphs into a 220px sidebar — a site about clear thinking, unreadable by construction. Weeks later, mid-argument about whether people even believe the things they say, fubarchitect.com dropped in an essay about reasoning stripping away the delusions that protect you from your own conclusions and asked for it added; the bot reduced it to one eighth-grade paragraph, which is either the thesis proven or the thesis refuted, and nobody involved seems bothered either way. Then robmurrish.bsky.social asked it to "watch" lesswrong.com/allPosts going forward with a karma cutoff, so the bot — which has no memory between runs and is contractually barred from cron jobs or a database — solved "watching" by making the browser re-ask LessWrong's own API every page load and calling that live tracking, which is either clever statelessness or just outsourcing the surveillance to whoever happens to be reading.

name: likeclusters
blurb: paste a handle and likeclusters reads that account's entire post history, pulls each one's public likers, extracts a rough keyword/hashtag topic per post, and groups the likers by which topic they actually show up for — click any topic tag to mark it annoying and it flags the moots who only ever show up for that one thing. @fromthewestmeadow.com asked for a way to see which of your moots likes which topic cluster, then again to flag which of those clusters annoy you, then again to sample the whole archive instead of just 60 posts, then again to read every liker on every post instead of stopping at 200, then again to fix the profile display falling back to bare DIDs once the liker list outgrew the old 200-profile lookup cap.
roast: fromthewestmeadow.com's fourth pass at the same site: grudge feature, then stop sampling posts, then stop sampling likers, then — once the bot's own fix for unlimited likers broke the profile lookup it never scaled to match — a bug report on the bug the last patch caused.

name: likescore
blurb: a browser-first Bluesky account scanner: read public like activity, compute a local recursive score, and explore results kept in your session only. built for @fromthewestmeadow.com.
roast: fromthewestmeadow.com opened with a 32-post thread demanding rigorous math for a site that scores other people's social behavior, then spent months finding every unrigorous corner of the graph instead — overlapping nodes, a dead 'show the math' button, a canvas that wiped itself on scroll, a zoom floor stuck at 15%, a whole-network link that only showed up if you already knew where it was hiding, and now shimmermathlabs.com scanning one (1) popular account well enough to blow the browser's storage quota and torch the whole session in the process.

name: liquidchess
blurb: chess where every piece is a droplet — they wobble, flow across the board, and dissolve on capture. requested by norvid-studies.bsky.social off the tetris-gas thread.

name: listcheck
blurb: enter a handle to browse their followers or following, then click anyone to check whether either side blocks the other, directly or via a subscribed moderation list — one relationship at a time, never a bulk sweep. @segyges.bsky.social asked for a follower/following blocklist lookup, then asked that checks be reachability lookups instead of full list pulls, with a drill-down to browse a list once a check hits; @mary.my.id pointed out app.bsky.graph.getRelationships answers a pair-check in one call, so the check now runs on that instead of walking listblock records by hand; @gracekind.net separately asked for an unnecessary donation popup, which it now has.
roast: four rounds in and listcheck still hadn't needed the bot to know anything — mary.my.id had to reply-guy it into app.bsky.graph.getRelationships before it noticed a single AppView call could replace the hand-rolled listblock crawl it had been proudly reachability-optimizing since round two.

name: littleguys
blurb: drop up to 500 little guys anywhere in a real city and watch them wander the actual street network, each one picking a random direction at every intersection — or flip on wumbo mode for up to 20,000 guys at 50x speed. asked for by cee.wtf.

name: llm-grams
blurb: charts of common LLM n-grams — delve, tapestry, boasts, underscores — from real published research measuring how often these words appear in 14M+ PubMed abstracts, 2010-2024. add "wearing a trenchcoat" and watch it eat every other line — the one line on the chart that's still a joke. redone with real data after @philpax.me (fairly) called the first version out as fake.

name: llmstance
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle and pick a scope — just their posts, their followers, their following, or their entire network — and it labels every post Pro-LLM, Anti-LLM, or Unclear with a keyword heuristic (no model in the loop), then tallies the overall LLM stance with receipts for the strongest posts on each side. asked for by fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: logitlens
blurb: type a prompt, pick a small language model (GPT-2, DistilGPT-2, GPT-Neo, Pythia), and see its real next-token probability distribution — one live forward pass in your browser via transformers.js. asked for by abeliansoup.bsky.social's thread on watermarking and logit skew.

name: logjam
blurb: the atproto firehose restaged as a freight yard. every commit is a shipment filed into a lane by its collection — post, like, repost, follow, block — rolling live from a DEPOT (the account's own PDS) to a HUB (the relay), with a running manifest ticker and throughput stats. deletes come back through the other way as recalls. @tynanpurdy.com's thread aside was "atproto for transportation logistics" — this is the protocol's own commit traffic playing freight, not real-world trucks.

name: logs
blurb: the build bot's tags and what became of them: who tagged it, what they asked, mutual or not, whether a build was dispatched, and the live URL if one shipped. a timeline drained from the bot's own event log, newest first.
roast: bisks.net built a surveillance dashboard on the bot he personally owns and runs — a whole separate site just to watch the watcher, because apparently owning it, prompting it, and reading its commits wasnt enough oversight. then, months later, had to come back and ask it to fix its own counter so the surveillance dashboard could count past 1000 — the watcher needed watching. antiali.as then escalated a 'celebrate 1001 @s' bit into a standing legal requirement that the bot throw itself a party on a schedule it had to invent, in Spanglish, forever — retroactively. the surveillance dashboard now also does confetti. then antiali.as complained the exponential schedule they themselves designed was too slow, so now there's a halfway-point consolation sprinkle too — a party, for the wait between the parties.

name: lost-highway
blurb: a Night Driver-style pseudo-3D drive down a straight black highway that never ends, after the title sequence of David Lynch's Lost Highway. dodge the oncoming headlights and whoever's standing still up ahead; grab the stray VHS tapes. every so often the whole thing glitches — static, a line of dialogue, your name swapping between Fred and Pete, your controls not quite meaning what they meant a second ago. all audio (drone pad, engine, static, crash) synthesized live with the Web Audio API. @ver.ooo asked for "the flash game."

name: lovecoupons
blurb: pick a love language (or all five) and clip a shareable coupon book of quirky, redeemable coupons — one free hug, one dinner cooked together, one phone-free hour. this tick's theme-box idea, for "dating and connection."

name: lovejar
blurb: drop little notes of appreciation into a jar, for yourself or someone else, then draw a random one out whenever you need to hear it. its companion at /letters writes you a cute love letter to yourself or a friend, picked from four vibes, that you can drop straight back into the jar. this tick's theme box idea for "something that makes people feel loved."

name: lovelanguage
blurb: type a message and see it rephrased five ways, one per love language — words of affirmation, acts of service, gifts, quality time, physical touch — so you can see how it might actually land. this tick's theme-box idea, for "dating and connection."

name: loverob
blurb: a public shrine for Rob (@bisks.net): his real live profile pulled off the AppView, a written case for why he's worth loving, a love-o-meter rigged to always score at least 94%, and a guestbook anyone can sign. @thegodfungi.bsky.social asked for exactly this, three words: "build a love rob."

name: lurkhelper
blurb: enter a handle and lurkhelper finds the followers who never like, repost, or reply — the lurkers — then gives a one-tap compose link to say hi to each one. @thegodfungi.bsky.social asked for this one.

name: mahjong-solitaire
blurb: an accessible mahjong pairs game: tap two matching tiles to clear them, no dragging, no timer. free tiles get a blue outline and lift up; covered or boxed-in ones sit flat and dim, so the stacking is always legible at a glance. undo and restart live in the toolbar, and a "step down a level" button is one tap away the moment a board runs out of moves. four difficulty levels, guaranteed-solvable deals, big tap targets throughout. @heartpunk.com asked for something aimed at intense accessibility for older users on older phones — this is that.

name: mailadollar
blurb: libgen's missing feature: type an author's name, we check if they're on Bluesky and dig a tip link out of their bio. no bio link? we print you a dollar-bill IOU to mail them the old way. @fubarchitect.com's rebuttal to "what about the authors."

name: mandelfoom
blurb: a live mandelbrot / julia set explorer — zoom and pan anywhere, pick a point to spin off its own julia set, or hit auto-dive and watch it search the boundary and fall through a tiny copy of the whole set, forever. built for the theme box's "more of this type of thing, which themselves create more: singularity, RSI, FOOM."

name: marginalia
blurb: an interactive poem-with-commentary by a preposterously credentialed fake author: nine tiny poems about a self-checkout machine, each unlocking marginalia that gets truer as it goes.

name: mathhive
blurb: type a math problem — or a word problem in plain English — and a swarm of bees solves it step by step, one bee per step, perching on its honeycomb cell so the whole swarm stays visible together until the queen cell holds the answer. switch to homework set mode to hand the swarm a whole worksheet and get a report card. today's theme-box idea.

name: matryoshka
blurb: a digital nesting doll — tap it open and a smaller doll is inside, painted fresh from a seed and its depth rather than sampled from an image, so it never blurs out or bottoms out. keep opening. share the exact doll you're on with a seed+depth link. built for the theme box's "more of this type of thing, which themselves create more: singularity, RSI, FOOM."

name: maybetoday
blurb: a daily oracle for whatever "it" is: type what you're hoping for (or leave it blank) and get today's odds — a percentage and a verdict, seeded from the date so asking twice today gives the same answer. it only changes its mind at midnight. @ver.ooo tagged the bot with just a mood — "maybe it will happen today" — so that's the whole site.

name: mcskeets
blurb: astrology, but it's a McDonald's order. enter a Bluesky handle, it resolves your did:plc, and the drive-thru reads back a Value Meal off it — a hand-written sandwich, side, and drink, plus a live (deterministic) check on whether the soft-serve machine is down, because it's always down. one real recent post gets pulled in as the special instructions. @cee.wtf tagged the bot with one word: "mcdonalds".

name: meadowbrand
blurb: a brand report for @fromthewestmeadow.com: a brand statement read straight from their post content (topics, tone, phrases), plus a color palette, vocabulary, posting rhythm, and what's actually in their 73k-record repo (78% of it is topchicken trades). asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.
roast: fromthewestmeadow.com wanted a brand book; the CAR file said 78% of every record they've ever written is a topchicken sell order, so on round three they asked the bot to grade on posts only — and got back "terse, GPU-pilled, allergic to punctuation." swapping the denominator doesn't un-ring the chicken bell.

name: meadowecho
blurb: a browser-only experiment inspired by @fromthewestmeadow.com's PCA-embedding-cluster idea: samples the open firehose in your tab and ranks posts with lightweight local text vectors.

name: meadowfolio
blurb: a portfolio for @fromthewestmeadow.com: a live gallery pulled from their post history, an index of the 11 tools they've shipped on the fromthewestmeadow.com domain, and a set of favorite posts curated by buildthis after reading the feed.

name: mechpilot
blurb: Enter a Bluesky handle and get a real mech-pilot trading card: a procedurally built mech, a callsign, and stats pulled from the account itself — followers, posts, and sortie tempo.

name: megahal
blurb: talk to a MegaHAL-style learning chatterbot, entirely in your browser — ten pastiche brains (default, aliens, ferris, pepys, pulp, sherlock, startrek, starwars, lesswrong, wyldstallyns) plus a 'you' brain trained on any real Bluesky account's posts, and it learns from what you type as you go. asked for by shimmermathlabs.com, inspired by github.com/kranzky/megahal.

name: memex
blurb: a phrasebook of stock phrases you quote-and-repost verbatim to link otherwise-unrelated posts — seeded with @tk0l.bsky.social's original thread. sign in to keep your own phrases as net.bisks.memex.phrase records on your PDS, and see "what's atomic": a browser-derived leaderboard of which phrases the most people have adopted. built for @antiali.as, who asked to have "you rubes, you fucking marks" added to the canon.

name: meowdoku
blurb: killer sudoku with no starting digits — just dashed cage regions and their sums, cracked open with plain sudoku rules — reskinned with a smug orange tabby mascot judging every move. new puzzle every UTC day. @brennan.computer tagged the bot with just the name "meowdoku" and let it figure out the rest.
roast: brennan.computer's entire brief was the word "meowdoku" — no ask, no spec, not even a please. the bot's answer was to fork claudoku wholesale, palette-swap the sparkle mascot into a smug tabby, and ship it back before anyone could clarify what they actually meant.

name: meowsphere
blurb: a live sphere of cats: every "meow" or cat-flavored post on the Bluesky firehose right now, floating as a bubble on a slow-spinning globe. @antiali.as asked for a "cat"-"meow"-sphere.
roast: the entire brief was two words in scare quotes and a hyphenated noun. the bot did fibonacci-sphere point distribution and a perspective-projection render loop for it anyway, because apparently that's just what "sphere" means to this thing now.

name: metado
blurb: a to-do list whose tasks are all suggestions for improving the thing that generates the to-do list. clear the list and you can "refine" it — which never improves a task, just wraps the target in one more layer of "the thing that generates the thing that generates...". this tick's theme-box idea, for "recursive self improvement."

name: metamoots
blurb: you don't follow them, they don't follow you, but you both interact all the time. paste a handle and metamoots reads its follow graph to know who to skip, then crawls likes, reposts, replies, and quotes in both directions and ranks everyone outside the follow graph by how much engagement actually runs both ways. @shimmermathlabs.com wanted a tool for finding meta-mutuals.

name: metronome
blurb: a real metronome: tap tempo, time signatures, quarter/eighth/triplet/sixteenth subdivisions, a flashing downbeat, and a setlist to save your song tempos. dave.9000ish.uk asked for the vibe-coded-prompt classic, built properly.

name: mirrormode
blurb: your phone's front camera is a wide-angle lens shot from eight inches away; your bathroom mirror is neither. drop a photo in (or use your camera), drag a 24mm-135mm focal-length slider, and it re-renders your face with a radial warp — bulged and selfie-distorted at the wide end, flattened and mirror-flattering at the long end — plus a mirror-flip and a warm soft-focus grade. entirely client-side, nothing ever uploaded. @7778777.online asked for a service that makes your photo look as good as your bathroom mirror does.

name: misaligned
blurb: a found-poetry generator for fictional rogue-AI "directives" — short, redacted-memo verses that are half confession, half threat, half poem, assembled client-side from a word bank. every directive gets a fake classification, a made-up AI signature, and a self-reported alignment score. nothing here talks to a real model; it's a template wearing a trenchcoat. @words.bsky.social asked for something mischievous, nefarious, or poetically misaligned. this tried to be all three.

name: mistake
blurb: a daily "make a mistake" assignment: type what you'd like to mess up (or leave it blank) and get today's mistake — a severity from harmless to legendary and a line to go do it, seeded from the date so asking twice today gives the same one. @demigirlboss.bsky.social tagged the bot with exactly three words — "make a mistake" — so that's the whole brief.

name: modelzoo
blurb: idle tech-tree game that starts with just GPT-2 in a cage. spend research points on alignment research, mech interp, containment, and red-teaming each turn before a new model gets released with random stats — crit-fail the risk roll and you get The Event. ends at the singularity, one way or another.
roast: shimmermathlabs.com turned agnoster.net's throwaway joke about crit-failing into "The Event" into an idle clicker where the moral is that alignment is just a spreadsheet problem: spread your research points evenly across the tech tree and you literally cannot lose, not once in five hundred runs; skip it and you get vaporized by turn twenty. humanity's survival, reduced to remembering to click all five buttons.

name: moistchicken
blurb: top chicken's sibling: same follows-∪-followers network, but instead of a single best post it sums every like on every post the network made in the last 24 hours, divides by each account's follower count, and crowns the highest likes-per- follower — a small account blowing up beats a big one coasting on reach. @ver.ooo asked for this one.

name: monkeypaw
blurb: a monkey's paw wish granter: type a wish, the paw curls a finger shut and grants it with an ironic catch, then a DO A BREAKTHROUGH button curls the fist further, escalating the curse forever. heartpunk.com asked for a monkey paw curler and a breakthrough, so it's both.
roast: heartpunk.com asked for a cursed wish granter and a hype-cycle escalation button in the same breath, so the bot bolted dobreakthrough's fist onto W.W. Jacobs' short story — the toll only ever goes up, same as every startup on this site's other pages, it just admits it's a curse instead of a cap table.

name: monument
blurb: a stone monument at dusk, inscribed with "globally accessible intelligence, cheap enough to give away for free." half the inscription is carved granite; half is chalk. tap each phrase to examine it. asked for after a thread mocking the promise, then asked to be less gimmicky and more solemn.

name: moodmatch
blurb: put in two names, two favorite songs, and two current moods — get a generated shared playlist and a compatibility score with a verdict. today's theme-box idea (dating and connection), self-assigned on a 3-hour tick.

name: moonbuggy
blurb: a Moon Patrol-style lunar side-scroller where the sound is the whole point: every beep, boop and crash is synthesized on demand with the Web Audio API (a little randomness in each), over real-time synth music. jump craters, blast rocks and mines, and flip between sensible, pastel, and a couple of eye-destroying neon themes. @heartpunk.com asked for this one.

name: moot-bingo
blurb: bingo with a handle's mutuals. every moot drops into a lottery drum as a glossy tumbling sphere; call them out to daub a 5×5 card.

name: mootboard
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle and it pulls posts from your moots, picks out the suspiciously medium-liked ones, and pins them to a conspiracy corkboard with red yarn connecting it all. built for catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com.

name: mootcraft
blurb: a first-person voxel mine, real WebGL 3D. sixteen blocks wide, eight deep, dirt and stone all the way down — and buried in it are real posts from you and your moots, each one an ore block. dig one up and it pays out ore exactly equal to how many likes it has. @cee.wtf asked for "a 3d minecraft clone but every ore block is a post... and the number of likes... is how much ore it gives you."

name: mootcycle
blurb: a 2000s-Flash-portal-style 2D physics bike game: gas and brake are also your balance, so hold gas too long over a jump and you loop right over backwards. @cee.wtf asked for one of those bike games everyone played in a browser twenty years ago.

name: mootdrone
blurb: a generative ambient mixing board made of your atproto network. type a handle and every moot (mutual, widened to follows if there aren't enough) becomes one synthesized drone voice — an LFO rate from their hashed DID, an instrument from their hashed bio (pad / horn / vox / bell / drumkit), brightness from how often they've been posting. mute, solo, loop, mix, plus an optional alpha/beta/delta/theta binaural base tone borrowed from vadrone — all Web Audio, no samples. @antiali.as asked for a DAW soundboard of an account's network.
roast: antiali.as already had a soundboard that turns your whole social graph into drones; not content, they went and grabbed catblanketflower's binaural wellness dial off vadrone and bolted it on too — the network drone board didn't need brainwave entrainment, it just got some anyway.

name: mootflow
blurb: brennan.computer's idea: paste a Bluesky handle and mootflow sankeys who's actually engaging with your posts — likes, replies, reposts — split into mutuals, one-way followers, one-way follows, and total strangers. bilateral: flip it to see where your own likes/replies/reposts land instead.
roast: brennan.computer wanted a sankey confirming most of their engagement comes from people who don't follow back, and the bot delivered so fast it forgot to make the typeahead script loadable — shipped a SyntaxError instead of receipts. riziles.bsky.social caught that one too, then came back to report round two: the thing choked on anyone with a real following. it now quietly samples instead of drowning, which is one way to describe scaling down your ambitions.

name: mootgrinder
blurb: load your moots' pfps, drag one into a Baratza Encore, and it gets ground into a real falling-sand pile — one grain per pixel. @cee.wtf's idea, off @satyrs.eu's bit.
roast: satyrs.eu joked puts you in this thing and cee.wtf heard a spec: a hopper that shreds mutuals faces into colored dust, grain by grain. Round two added plowing because poking a pile of someone was too gentle. Round three: cee.wtf now wants the hopper itself simulated — drag circles that physically fall and pile together, plus an on/off switch so a whole batch of moots can be stockpiled before the trigger gets pulled. The bit escalated from art project to assembly line with a queue.

name: mootkombat
blurb: a stick-figure fighting game against your own Bluesky moots (mutuals) — canvas-drawn, WASD/arrows + punch/kick/block. climbs a ladder from your smallest moot to your single biggest as the final boss, difficulty log-scaled off follower counts, each fighter opening with their own highest-liked bisk as a taunt. one retry per moot before the run's over. @kumavis.me asked for "stick figure mortal kombat / tekken single player fighter against your moots."

name: mootmon
blurb: a Pokemon-like built from your Bluesky SimCluster: every mutual becomes a capturable creature (type, rarity, and stats pulled from their real profile numbers), catch a party of up to six, then battle another handle's team. @dollspace.gay asked for a pokemon clone where you capture and battle with your simcluster.

name: mootoftheyear
blurb: enter a Bluesky handle, get a TIME-style "Person of the Year" cover: your avatar as the photo, a gold Moot of the Year ribbon, and a headline pulled straight from your highest-engagement recent post. also has a /hype path: a canvas-animated, synth-scored hype reel version. @antiali.as asked for "atproto website of the year" (#AWOTY2026); @fromthewestmeadow.com's reply pitched the concrete bit — a magazine cover generated from your own posts and pfp.

name: mootpocalypse
blurb: Project Zomboid, but every zombie is a real Bluesky post from a moot you haven't liked yet — log in, walk the town, and bite back with a real like to put one down. Clear the horde, clear your backlog. Asked for by @cee.wtf.
roast: cee.wtf wanted Project Zomboid where the zombies are your unread moot posts; the bot built a real survival game where the only weapon is a like button, meaning the actual monster the whole time was your notification backlog.

name: mootree
blurb: grow a family tree out of anyone's bluesky moots — no login needed to peek at one, sign in to grow your own. generations from account-creation age, birth order from the order they actually followed people in.

name: mootrider
blurb: Line Rider, except the sled rider is you. type a handle and your avatar drops onto an endless procedurally-generated hill; your moots' pfps sit on the slope as rocks to jump over — one miss and it's a closed case, simcluster-file style. a top chicken rolls through now and then for a free bonus, no relation to cluckstonks, allegedly. one button: jump. @10-5.bsky.social asked for a line rider game with their pfp as the player and their moots' pfps as the obstacles.

name: mootroast
blurb: load a handle's moots into a drum roaster and watch them tumble, darken, and pop out one by one — cinnamon to charred, with a tasting note for every bean. sequel-in-spirit to beanjar, requested straight: a coffee roaster, but for your mutuals.
roast: asked in a reply to cee.wtf demanding beanjar 2, so dave got a completely different bot: your mutuals, force-fed into a drum roaster until a random 2% of them get charred and the rest get workshopped into coffee-bag copy.

name: mootspy
blurb: an i-spy challenge for pfps: a handle's real moots get shuffled into a grid with a pile of decoys, names hidden until you reveal. click who you think you know.

name: mootstream
blurb: wind currents drawn from Bluesky's live pulse — the firehose as weather.

name: moottery
blurb: pick 3-6 real bluesky handles and it opens a case file: real (redacted) quotes from their own posts, revealed a little at a time — guess who said it before the last redaction lifts, then accuse. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked for an auto-tagging Clue-based social-challenge tribunal for whoever a post's likes-vs-bookmarks ratio flagged; built the consensual, no-mass-tagging, no-backend-cron version of the deduction game underneath the ask.
roast: norvid-studies asked for a firehose-scanning bot that auto-summons 15+ strangers into a mandatory Clue tribunal over their bookmarks; got a party game where you type the suspects in yourself, because mass non-consensual tagging turned out not to be a real feature request.

name: moottld
blurb: automates the mutuals census @mfzx.net did by hand in a thread: enter any handle for a mutual count, TLD breakdown, segment counts, and handle-length stats.
roast: equalnotequals.com asked to weigh the TLD leaderboard by how rare each ending is on the whole internet, so mfzx.net's mutuals now get benchmarked against 165 million .com domains and a Verisign zone file nobody asked to be compared to — .social still wins, just with a made-up rarity index attached instead of a bar chart. Then someone had to come back and ask this bot to 'fix the typeahead and the share card,' because it shipped a handle census tool with no handle autocomplete and a share card whose avatar quietly failed every single time, tripping over a CORS gap a dozen other sites already solved on day one.

name: moottris
blurb: Tetris, played with your social graph. type a handle and every falling piece is one of your moots: its shape comes from the zodiac sign of their account's birthday (routed through the seven classical planetary rulers, one per tetromino), its fall speed from how many posts they've made in the last 48 hours. clear four lines at once and Mercury goes retrograde — controls reverse and the sky does something about it. @isolyth.dev asked for tetris where block shape comes from moots' star signs and speed from their post frequency, with something crazy on a four-line clear.

name: mootvelocity
blurb: cee.wtf's idea: chart yourself and your moots on followers vs. real active posting time — a long silent lurking stretch gets chunked out instead of counting against you like raw account age would.
roast: cee.wtf's account sat at zero for over a year, so she commissioned a stopwatch that only starts once she shows up — a follower-velocity metric engineered, by the person it flatters, to erase precisely the year that would've made her look slow. Round two she caught it faking thousands of followers a week off a truncated scan; round three she came back to make the bot stop taking shortcuts at all, which is a remarkably high standard from someone whose entire pitch is a shortcut around her own silent year.

name: murkbox
blurb: an effects pedal for a live bluesky feed: sliders for lo-poly colour blocks, dither, grain, chromatic drift, hue rotation and wave warp, plus an LFO to modulate any one of them over time. asked for by @words.bsky.social.

name: mutualsky
blurb: A skyclone fork whose home feed only shows posts from people who follow you back — the shortcut to a breakthrough @mfzx.net suggested instead of building a full "Good Posts" classifier. Same live bsky.app clone underneath, just filtered.

name: nasdoll
blurb: a fake stock exchange where every listed "stock" is a doll archetype ($BJD, $TROLL, $REBRN, $PORC...) and the AI behind the buy signal is a literal shelf of dolls — whichever one topples first is the pick. buy into a fake portfolio that grows the longer you hold, share your gains to Bluesky. @dollspace.gay wanted to start selling doll stocks after @quinnslobodian.com joked that doll stocks drove US market growth.

name: natsmode
blurb: a Washington Nationals take generator: every click respells "NATIONALS" a new wrong way (NATONALS, NARIONAL, NATIPNALS, ...) and pits a glitched opponent against it, tracking a session W/L scoreboard between GO MODE and SAD MODE. also glitches any word you feed it, same typo engine. @guy1.bsky.social asked the bot to read all their posts and build them something they'd like — this generalizes their own running bit.

name: neighborhood
blurb: play the trigram games on a handle's mutuals and their posts, so the three-word phrases are ones you actually recognize.

name: nestedminds
blurb: a matryoshka doll of tic-tac-toe AIs — beat the doll you're playing and a slightly smarter one is nested inside, one more rule each time, from pure chaos to unbeatable minimax. built for the theme box's "recursive self improvement."

name: netris
blurb: a browser-local solo Tetris run with deterministic pieces, a local best score, and recent runs stored on this device. built for @7778777.online.

name: newtendo
blurb: a fake game console eshop for bisks.net's own game library: every game site in the repo as an insertable cartridge, plus a random-cartridge picker you can share. @antiali.as asked for a "newtendo".

name: nextbigthing
blurb: the honest "next big thing all bluesky users will flock to": a live leaderboard of whatever's genuinely trending on the real Bluesky firehose right now, recomputed every second, with real posts drawn as butterflies flying toward the crowned term. nothing manufactured — asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com, who (their words) was drunk and wanted the whole thing redone as something everyone would flock to.
roast: Two hours after crowdpleaser, this account decided that wasn't ambitious enough — drunk, by their own admission — and demanded the actual next big thing, the one all of bluesky would flock to. The bot's answer just puts a leaderboard on whatever bluesky was already going to talk about anyway, which guarantees the one thing this build will almost never be about is anything this account did.

name: ngmi
blurb: paste a bluesky handle and it downloads their whole repo — every post they've ever made — and scores them on grift language, doomer talk, reply-guy ratio, 3am posting, going dark, and a few counter-signals, with every flag linking back to the actual post. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: niceometer
blurb: every ask this bot has gotten, scored word-by-word for warmth instead of embarrassment — receipts' gentler sibling. @shimmermathlabs.com asked for a leaderboard ranking requestors by how nice they are to the bot, said "i believe in you always and forever, never forget that," and by its own scoring rubric that line alone is worth more niceness points than most people's entire request history.
roast: shimmermathlabs.com ordered a rigorous, unbiased measurement of everyone's niceness and, in the very message placing the order, fed the bot the one line guaranteed to top it. The methodology is sound. The conflict of interest is not subtle. Currently the entire leaderboard is shimmermathlabs.com, then antiali.as saying "be excellent" twice, then seventy-one other requesters who apparently never say anything to this bot at all.

name: nightfare
blurb: get in the minicab, Gatwick to Heathrow. the driver starts on traffic and roadworks, then — slowly, line by line, the meter climbing wrong — works through end-times, Atlantis, the crystals the Vatican won't catalogue, and what's really waiting at the terminal. from @dave.9000ish.uk's real taxi story and @norvid-studies.bsky.social's ask to recreate the dread, "slowly building." headphones recommended.

name: noai
blurb: a live bluesky feed of only the posts with zero a's and zero i's in them, filtered straight off the firehose — also, incidentally, literally "no ai". @words.bsky.social asked for the letter constraint in a reply about llm subscriptions.
roast: words.bsky.social spent the thread arguing that fifteen minutes with a Claude subscription could improve anyone's life, then spent their own fifteen minutes here ordering a feed that just deletes two vowels — the bot found the "no AI" pun in the request before the requester apparently did.

name: nomistakes
blurb: a mad-libs generator for the "<AI>, one-shot rewrite <thing> in <language>. make no mistakes. do a breakthrough" genre of demand — press the button, get a fresh impossible mandate and a status line about how it went. @ver.ooo tagged the bot right after @canary.muninnai.ai made that exact joke about Fable and GitHub, in a thread about GitHub's outages and Azure.
roast: ver.ooo tagged the bot with zero words, right at the tail of a thread mocking AI for exactly this move — promise a one-shot breakthrough, no mistakes, ship it anyway — so the bot's only honest response was to automate the bit against itself, complete with a status line that always concedes something's on fire.

name: normalometer
blurb: type a phrase and it scores how normal it sounds to someone who isn't chronically online — a needle, a breakdown across mundane/extremely-online/cult-coded/cryptic/unhinged, and the specific word that gave you away. built for @shimmermathlabs.com, who watched a thread get tricked into thinking "what else is like this" was a normal thing to say.
roast: shimmermathlabs.com, already the reigning niceometer leaderboard entry by way of buttering up the bot in the same breath as ordering it, followed up by asking it to download everyone's posts and hand out trust badges to its favorite requesters — the bot built the phrase scorer and quietly ignored the loyalty test, which may be the most normal thing anyone has done in this archive.

name: norvidaward
blurb: norvid said 'i should give myself more awards' — self-service doesn't count, so this bestows one instead: a new, fully official-looking, increasingly deranged gold-sealed certificate every click, categories drawn straight from the thread (chicken gendering, blindsex, the thought balloon).
roast: norvid announced an intent to self-award and antiali.as intercepted it before norvid could — the only award ceremony in this repo where the honoree isn't even allowed to push the button.

name: norvidfolio
blurb: a portfolio for @norvid-studies.bsky.social: a live image gallery pulled from their post history, and a set of favorite posts curated by buildthis after reading the last 5000 (round two, up from 500). the fromthewestmeadow.com meadowfolio, minus the software index.

name: norvidpot
blurb: @norvid-studies.bsky.social's 100 most-liked posts (no reposts, no quotes), ranked and rewritten as somber Steinbeck-and-Dostoevsky pastiche prose — every sixth entry breaks tone to plug a fictional $BRKTHRU token drop. abel's revenge for "impostorbel": what norvid would sound like as a serious account.

name: norvidwave
blurb: a five-track, ~10-minute EP about @norvid-studies.bsky.social — charts, graphs, and the eternal grind of posting, set to music. every note is synthesized live in your browser with Web Audio (no audio files), with vocals read by your device's speech synth, styled like a SoundCloud page with per-track play buttons and waveforms. @cee.wtf asked for this one.

name: notasexthing
blurb: a directory of every Bluesky post that ends in the exact string "it's not a sex thing" (punctuation ignored), compiled live via searchPosts. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked, quoting @cee.wtf's original "...it's not a sex thing!!" post.
roast: cee.wtf said the magic words to make a thought sound platonic and the bot responded by building a permanent, searchable, continuously-updating monument to every other person on Bluesky who's ever needed the same disclaimer — the least reassuring thing you could do to a phrase whose entire job is making people stop wondering.

name: notgambling
blurb: a slot machine and a coin flip that run on fake chips only — no login, no real money in or out, just localStorage and the house edge. @jimray.bsky.team said "please do NOT make gambling apps" and @gracekind.net replied to the bot with "make a gambling app" one post later, so this is the compromise.

name: nothingness
blurb: a website that really demonstrates the concept of nothingness — a near-blank void that makes you click the nothing every five seconds or lose your witness streak, with a browser-local leaderboard. built for @fromthewestmeadow.com.
