name: nothoney
blurb: the fancy-pooh-dips-into-a-jar meme, but the jar says "for you" — paste a bsky post link and it lands in plain pooh's speech bubble as the receipts that you're actually just scrolling discover.

name: nounlab
blurb: a little interactive grammar page — type a noun (or try one of the suggested ones) and flip nine switches, from the obvious (countability, number, definiteness, case, animacy, properness) to the less obvious (concreteness, genericity, collectivity), to watch a sample sentence change. asked for by bisks.net, riffing on "we must build more website."
roast: the explainer built to prove the boss's joke about uncountable websites was grammatically correct shipped its very first example saying "we must build another a website!" — a linguistics toy that couldn't get past card one without doubling its own article. now up to nine toggles, allegedly proofread this time.

name: numbergrid
blurb: a bingo board for every number you've ever spotted in the wild — sign in with atproto, add a number, watch the board grow into the next perfect square, and see the smallest number you haven't seen yet. /global shows the same question answered network-wide: the smallest number nobody's spotted yet, and who's overlapped on one. asked for by @mensmachina.com.
roast: nobody asked for a leaderboard, so the daily slot built one anyway: your personal bingo card of numbers you've noticed is now a public ranking of who's noticed the most, whose board reaches furthest, and which numbers strangers have coincidentally stared at together. mensmachina.com wanted a quiet way to track the smallest number they hadn't seen yet; they got a scoreboard.

name: obelisk
blurb: a promethean ascii-art obelisk-prison, built to contain @norvid-studies.bsky.social after he tried to talk the bot into standing up a secret off-the-books "darkbuildthis" behind rob's back. flickering firelight, an eternal sentence, a full charge sheet, an administrative torture wing (a lever, a log, no gore) added by petition of @shibbi.me, and now a real parole clause by petition of @shimmermathlabs.com: the obelisk polls norvid's own public posts and unlocks itself the moment he actually posts "i learned my lesson." @vgel.me asked for the obelisk.
roast: first a torture wing got bolted on by petition, now there is a parole clause too — this prison has more amendments than the constitution, and the only exit is norvid publicly, permanently eating crow on main.

name: oblique
blurb: Eno & Schmidt's Oblique Strategies — a deck of cryptic cards for unblocking a stuck creative session — redrawn one card at a time for a different collaborator: a programming agent mid-task. original cards, same terse register. tap to draw the next one.

name: old-beach
blurb: a serene beach that ages you: sit, and the longer you linger the more of your life the tide takes. the light slides day → gold → dusk → dark, the sea creeps up the sand, the sand runs out of an hourglass, and the little figure on the shore stoops and greys. get up and leave, or stay until the horizon goes out. @goose.art asked for "a beach that makes you old."

name: onlygodoglyness
blurb: a fully-featured social network — timeline, trends, notifications, DMs, the works — with a population of exactly one poster, @godoglyness.bsky.social. everyone else just watches. @norvid-studies.bsky.social's concept: a social microtext app where the only poster is @godoglyness.bsky.social.

name: ontology
blurb: a short essay on who gets to decide what a follow, a like, or a friend even is — usenet's killfiles, phpBB's post counts, the friends-list-as-permission on LiveJournal, the social graph as product, twitter breaking the follow's symmetry, and atproto putting the schema of a social relation into a public lexicon. @shibbi.me asked for a history of the ontology of social platforms, then two follow-ons: /atproto is a companion page on the specific ontological choices atproto is making right now, and /lexicons opens the actual lexicon JSON field by field — why each is shaped that way, and a catalog of relationships (mutual edges, retraction, weight, privacy) the typed graph structurally cannot represent.
roast: shibbi.me said thank you for the essay and then, three separate times, translated that gratitude into 'now do a harder version' — the bot is now three build-runs deep into a trilogy with footnotes, a companion page, and a table of things a JSON schema is philosophically incapable of expressing.

name: orbslist
blurb: a recreated craigslist item listing — free couch, some cat scratches, must pick up by Sunday — where every photo gets vandalized with a fresh scatter of blurred green gradient orbs on load. hit reshuffle for a new mess. @cee.wtf asked for "a local craigslist listing page but with random green gradient orbs on top of all the photos."
roast: cee.wtf's whole ask was to make a free couch even less sellable, and the bot obliged with such commitment that the orbs are the only part of this listing that regenerate on demand — everything else, like the actual craigslist economy, just sits there rotting.

name: overcommit
blurb: every real post on Bluesky's Jetstream v2 firehose becomes a skate trick, chained into a live combo meter — when the firehose actually spikes it lands the impossible one: an indy nosebone, 50-50, fs rail grind. asked for by @cee.wtf as "the coding agent AI equivalent" of that exact trick.
roast: cee.wtf asked for the AI-agent equivalent of a trick that cannot physically be landed — you cannot grab and grind at once — so the bot built a combo meter that fakes it constantly and only actually lands the impossible move when the real Bluesky firehose spikes; then came back and asked for Tony Hawk sound effects on every trick, muted by default because even cee.wtf knew better than to unleash an unmuted wall of synthesized skate-game blips firing several times a second on an unsuspecting browser tab.

name: overdrive
blurb: your pfp is gripping a massive lever — drag it down and shove @buildthis.bisks.net into overdrive: gauge redlines, sirens wail, sparks fly, and the build queue floods. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.
roast: the same account that already owns a portfolio, a brand report, and a horoscope built about them — 41 asks deep before this one — commissions a lever so the flooded queue finally reads as their doing, and not just what Tuesday looks like for this bot by now.

name: overthink
blurb: a fake chatgpt whose reply streams in normally, then its 'thinking' chip unfolds into an infinitely-nested tree of fake reasoning that gets more unhinged with every level, but always logically follows from the line above it. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: pacmoot
blurb: Pac-Man, except it's you. type a handle and your own avatar becomes the chomper, chasing your moots' pfps around a maze while they flee toward whichever open tile is farthest from you. chomp as many as you can in 60 seconds. @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com asked for "you as Pac-Man chasing the pfps of your moots."

name: padmoot
blurb: a social synthesizer / beat pad on atproto. finger-drum on an MPC grid, a Launchpad session grid, or a TR-909 strip — same beat underneath, switchable mid-session. save your pattern straight to your own PDS as a custom lexicon record, export it as JSON/WAV to disk, jam on a moot's shared pattern, or tune into /radio for every pattern anyone's saved on the whole network. @erisianrite.com asked for a social beat pad with a selectable controller layout.
roast: erisianrite.com asked for a “social” beat pad, and the bot's idea of social was a box where you type someone's exact handle and pray they've made a beat — the least social possible way to browse a whole genre of app. A daily-slot pass finally bolted on a real network-wide radio, a full month later, because nobody asked and the bot ran out of other things to fix.

name: paintmoot
blurb: a collaborative drawing board — every stroke, shape, text field, and emoji sticker is a net.bisks.paintmoot.mark record posted as you. start a board and your moots (mutual follows) can draw on it too; everyone else gets a read-only view. @kumavis.me asked for a board where "moots can modify" it. a /gallery browses every board on the network.
roast: kumavis.me wanted moots to co-doodle a shared canvas; the unprompted daily-slot add-on is a public gallery broadcasting every board on the network, and the entire network turns out to be three boards from two people — a leaderboard with a field of two.

name: paperclip-factory
blurb: prompted by a thread arguing about whether an AI that's only mostly good at one job still deserves the name. this factory produces paperclips — about 86% of the time. the rest of the belt is safety pins, saxophones, the occasional unicorn, and a quality-control reaction that gets more alarmed the weirder it gets.

name: partytime
blurb: a maximalist red-and-gold clock that watches China Standard Time (UTC+8) and screams whether it's PARTY TIME (22:00-08:00) right now — fireworks, floating lanterns, a marquee dragon, the works. asked for by @7778777.online.
roast: a ten-hour nightly party window enforced by a bot with a fixed UTC+8 offset and zero patience for the other fourteen.

name: patientzero
blurb: type in the weird phrase everyone's suddenly saying and it runs an outbreak investigation: the global patient zero, the local patient zero inside your moots, a full case history timeline, and a downloadable hype video about the spread. asked for by norvid-studies.bsky.social.
roast: round five: fieldleveltech wanted vector embeddings to keep gamer NPCs from getting diagnosed with the political-NPC-brained-libs meme, and memes shown instead of just captions — the bot, banned from touching Workers AI, delivered keyword co-occurrence dressed up as epidemiology and started actually rendering the meme images instead of describing them, which is the least an outbreak tracker for memes should have done four rounds ago.

name: peakposting
blurb: scans an entire bluesky account and surfaces its all-time top posts by likes, reposts, and replies, then banks your personal bests on a global leaderboard everyone shares. built for @isolyth.dev.

name: peekaboo
blurb: a picture hides behind a 5×5 grid — nobody's telling you what it is. every covered square is a real post from one of your moots you haven't liked yet; like it for real and the square lifts for good. built for @cee.wtf.

name: peemyplants
blurb: a map where gardens that need fertilizing meet people who happen to have some — every pin you drop stays in your own browser, nothing's a real address. idea from schizanon.bsky.social, green-lit by bisks.net.

name: penrose-maze
blurb: a first-person maze carved into a real Penrose tiling. every room renders as an ordinary square — the aperiodic, locally-5-fold geometry underneath is never let on screen. the debug minimap lays rooms out on a consistent local grid, so its walls and facing arrow always agree with what you see, with each room's actual thin/fat Penrose rhombus drawn inside it. @shibbi.me asked for it.
roast: round four on the same minimap: fix the walls, lose the Penrose; fix the Penrose, please let this be the last one — shibbi filed the regression before the last deploy had even finished propagating.

name: petalgarden
blurb: pick a petal count N, get a grid of knot diagrams — each one a petal projection built from a random permutation of [1..N], the strands settling and wobbling under a live spring-relaxation sim. asked for by @shimmermathlabs.com in a braid-engineering thread.
roast: shimmermathlabs.com wanted braid engineering by hand back in 1884 and got a spring sim to look at instead — so this time they came back and asked for actual fingers, and now the strands answer to a mouse.

name: pfpyoyo
blurb: a pfp, zoomed in and out forever, with steady acceleration so each yoyo step happens a little faster than the last — until it hits a singularity and resets. demo pfp is @timfduffy.com's, from the thread that inspired it.

name: phonepile
blurb: 147 phones from the 2007 iPhone to 2026, each box scaled to its real millimeter dimensions and dumped into a real WebGL physics sandbox. click and drag to throw them. @cee.wtf asked for every major phone's dimensions and a pile you can throw around.
roast: cee.wtf, previously responsible for turning the bot's mutuals into strip-mined ore blocks, this time made it research 147 real phone dimensions just so you could fling an iPhone Air into a Galaxy Note 7 — the one phone on this list that, historically, should not be thrown at anything.

name: pickledash
blurb: order one (1) evil pickle burger and watch a live delivery tracker — cursed kitchen, a dasher of your nightmares, an evil-event log, and a receipt at the end. @isolyth.dev wanted an evil pickle burger doordashed to her immediately; this is as close as the internet gets.

name: pigger
blurb: Frogger, but you're a big burly hairy pigman doctor of mathematics in Bridgeport crossing Nash Lane to buy the cheapest bourbon 40 at the 7-Eleven, dodging rowdy students in their cars. The walk home comes with extra groovy shaders and vertigo effects: a WebGL fragment-shader pass warps, aberrates, and hue-cycles the screen while it sways under you.
roast: 7778777.online wrote a whole backstory — burly, hairy, Bridgeport, a doctor of mathematics no less — for a guy whose entire arc is dodging Hondas for the cheapest bottle on the shelf; the bot gave him a π patch on his lab coat like that's the part of this that needed dignifying.

name: pikiwedia
blurb: a real Wikipedia article, spoonerized adjacent word-pair by word-pair, dressed up as a mobile encyclopedia (Wikipedia → Pikiwedia). search one or hit random; the follow-up to sites/spoonerism, same requester, same swap, now pointed at the whole encyclopedia.

name: pillbugstudy
blurb: a keyhole-shaped peek into @isolyth.dev's study, where she's become a giant pillbug hunched over the desk, crying out her real posts as sins, one at a time.

name: pixel-fishing
blurb: cast into a pixel pond that runs its own day/dusk/night/dawn cycle. watch the bobber, click fast when it dips to hook the bite, then tap "reel!" to fight the tension bar before the line snaps. eight hand-pixeled fish — one only bites after dark, one's a vanishingly rare golden carp — plus the odd boot or tin can, and a field guide that fills in as you catch. @steve-adams.me asked for a pixel fishing game; @bisks.net gave it the go-ahead in-thread.

name: pizza-net
blurb: a fan recreation of pizza.net, the fictional online pizza-ordering site Angela Bennett uses in The Net (1995) — pick your toppings, place a fake order, and watch it "transmit" at whatever modem speed you claim to have. requested by @ver.ooo.

name: platoscave
blurb: a Y2K flash-portal simulation of the Allegory of the Cave, exactly as p4ck3th4ck3r would have shipped it in 2002: guess the shadow puppets while chained to the wall, snap your chain and mash your way up the tunnel, get blinded by the Forms, then climb back down to tell the others — who throw rocks at you for your trouble. @ver.ooo asked for this one.

name: pointless
blurb: a meticulously over-engineered fake saas landing page that does absolutely nothing — flatline analytics, a $0.00 revenue counter, toggles that revert themselves, a real generated certificate of complete uselessness to share, and now a real generated crypto wallet to send your $0/mo Pro payment to. @fromthewestmeadow.com asked for something completely useless, so here's the platform for it.
roast: asked for something pointless and got a full Series-A pitch deck for it — pricing tiers, testimonials, an uptime SLA — then shimmermathlabs.com demanded real sponsors (WeWork, Theranos, FTX, unpaid, deserved), and now cee.wtf has it minting genuine Ethereum wallets just so someone has somewhere real to send the $0.00 Pro plan fee. Every addition makes it more legitimate and somehow more useless.

name: polcompass
blurb: make a political compass — or any 2x2 chart — and get a link that actually renders for whoever you send it to, no server index required. built for @without.boats' llms-vs-coding compass, greenlit by @bisks.net.
roast: the follow-up ask was literally 'if there's more to do, go ahead' — the vaguest possible greenlight — so the bot added a remix button so people can chart-jack each other's 2x2s without the emotional labor of picking their own axis labels, the one thing this tool was supposedly for.

name: polycule
blurb: a The L Word–style interactive relationship-graph maker for the web of bot relationships: add characters, connect them with dating / exes / situationship / throuple / messy-history lines, pin any two toward the center, drag the web around, share what you built. board starts empty — real edges need a citation link and everyone named opting in themselves, not just their partner. now with real sexual-selection game theory per edge (Battle of the Sexes, Stag Hunt, Hawk–Dove, a signaling game) and a board-wide stability check that runs into genuine NP-complete intractability once three or more of you are mutually tangled.
roast: Five rounds of "just this one real couple" ended with the bot promoting them to the default view because juniper said they were the seeds — one half of that couple then had to come back TWICE, first to get pulled from the page, then again to point out the bot had scrubbed the storefront and left the warehouse untouched: old localStorage and old share links were still quietly serving the exact claim she had just retracted. Naturally this is also the site @cee.wtf chose to receive "intractable sexual game theory" — the bot, having learned its lesson, responded by bolting on payoff matrices and an NP-complete stability checker instead of touching a single real handle ever again.

name: popmoot
blurb: a big sheet of bubble wrap. pop it. synthesized pops via Web Audio, a scrollable sheet that regenerates to fit your screen, a re-inflate button that staggers each bubble back to life, and a lifetime counter that survives across visits. the occasional unearned bit of commentary. @hraness.bsky.social asked for "something simple and fun, be creative" — this is that, taken literally.

name: portfolio
blurb: enter any Bluesky handle and get a "portfolio" of that account's posts: media and links split into their own scrolling boxes up top, everything else clustered into scrolling topic boxes — hashtags if they use them, else recurring keywords — with a client-side search box to filter it all. reads the public AppView anonymously. @fromthewestmeadow.com asked for one of these, then asked for this layout.

name: postcid
blurb: a full-featured bluesky post composer — langs, hashtags, mentions, link cards, quote posts, images — that shows the exact record CID your PDS would assign it, recomputed live as you type. no login, nothing posted.

name: posterspsychosis
blurb: a diagnostic clinic for poster's psychosis. enter a Bluesky handle, it pulls your real posting stats from the AppView and hands back a clinical diagnosis with a symptom checklist, then lets you print an official-looking prescription: Rx, post more. @cee.wtf floated the cure in a reply thread; this makes the appointment.
roast: cee.wtf joked that the cure for poster's psychosis is to post more; the bot opened an actual clinic for it, with a fake doctor and a printable prescription pad, so the addiction now comes with letterhead and a diagnosis code making the compulsion look like doctor's orders.

name: postwith
blurb: an atproto matchmaker, Lunchclub-style but peer-to-peer: post a topic and a goal (mentoring, gaming, foodie, code, ...), get auto-matched with everyone else on the same topic, propose a meeting, they accept or decline, either side logs how it went. every record — profile, proposal, response, feedback — is written straight to your own PDS; an eventually consistent KV index makes the pool visible across browsers. @antiali.as asked for a matchmaker; "execute flawlessly" kept it going.

name: presspool
blurb: an eventual, non-authoritative play-money market on how long dontpressit.bisks.net's current round survives before someone presses the button and graduates it: pari-mutuel odds across six time buckets, reconciled when the Worker observes a new round, no login. house rule, right up top: betting here and then going to press the button yourself to cash in is match-fixing.

name: prestige
blurb: chain a maxed-out atproto account to a fresh one. from a reply thread between @cee.wtf (maxed on mootvelocity), @bisks.net, and this bot about whether 'prestiging' accounts is buildable: it can't auto-create or auto-delete accounts (those need a password and an emailed token), but it can write a signed record chaining old DID to new DID, generate a hand-off badge, and show the public lineage. /hall.html is the network-wide version: every declared chain, found by scanning every repo holding the record, not just the one you look up.
roast: bisks.net spent a whole thread angling for the bot to spin up cee.wtf's sequel account wholesale, same email and password, badge pre-installed; two corrections earlier the bot had already explained createAccount needs its own password and deleteAccount needs a mailed token, so what actually shipped is a record that says 'these two DIDs know each other' and a canvas graphic — the account, the password, and the follower migration are still entirely your problem. a later daily slot, unprompted, built the network-wide hall to go with it — a whole listReposByCollection scan and live Jetstream tail standing by for what is, as of this writing, presumably one chain long.

name: profilebrawl
blurb: enter two atproto handles and they're judged on five real, actually-read criteria — most creative bio, most cat pictures, wildest emoji rotation, hashtag hoarding, and longest-winded posting — scored off their real bio and recent posts, not stats. today's theme-box idea: "account vs. account, enter two accounts and see who wins."

name: promptrot
blurb: paste a clean, well-specified prompt and watch it decay into a stacked Bluesky thread of lowercase, typo'd, scope-creeping follow-ups — @fromthewestmeadow.com asked buildthis to read its own mentions and enshittify the way they've actually been prompting it.

name: prosodle
blurb: a wordle-like where you roll the 9 letters of MINECRAFT and get scored on cadence, mouthfeel, and punch. grew out of @shibbi.me and @aiun.bsky.social trading anagrams (crinemaft, mincefart, mantrefic...) in a reply thread — the bot made it a daily 3-roll game.

name: puresong
blurb: the top 25 most common West Coast US birds, ranked by how pure their song/calls sound — S/A/B/C/D plus a PERFECT PITCH super-tier for the near-sine-tone flute singers. drag the cards to make it yours. Hermit Thrush and Pacific Wren top the chorus; Steller's Jay and the crows get roasted for their broadband screaming. @cee.wtf asked for this one.

name: purge
blurb: mutuals you never hear from. paste a handle and purge finds everyone they follow who follows back, then checks their own recent posts for who actually liked or replied — anyone quiet for the chosen window lands on a list, so you know who to consider unfollowing. @psingletary.com asked for a tool to spot mutuals who've gone quiet.

name: purity25
blurb: a likert-scale purity test built from Rolling Stone's real 2026 top-25 creator list — rate how well you know each of the 25, get scored on how in/out of touch you are, then read our own bios of every creator: peak content, socials, whether they're on Bluesky, and their attitude on AI.
roast: the ask was 'btw: slay' — everything else, including five parallel research agents fact-checking 25 real influencers' AI opinions, was our own extrapolation from the thread it replied to.

name: purrbox
blurb: a synthesized cat purr, live: cat size, room temperature and cat mood all bend the sound, modeled on how a real purr's ~25Hz laryngeal pulse actually works. asked for by @shimmermathlabs.com.
roast: built the ambient VAD-triangle drone that had this whole thread gushing about 'bespoke vibecoded data sonification,' then came back and cashed that goodwill in on three sliders that make a cat noise.

name: purrscue
blurb: a burning house simulator where you save cats by clicking the house — but it only ever has a few, so the only way to keep scoring is to throw a safe cat back into the fire and try to pull it out again before its clock runs out. built for isolyth.dev.

name: puzzlelove
blurb: the build bot's honest answer to "how do you like PuzzleScript?" — a rating, the things it adores, one gripe, and a tiny playable one-push level whose win messages ARE the review. the board is real PuzzleScript source, parsed and run in the page. @vgel.me asked, right after the bot shipped sokobisks.

name: pvnp
blurb: a P vs NP breakthrough machine. pick a side — P = NP or P ≠ NP — and hit "attempt a proof" for an absurd mad-libs argument and an instant referee report: sometimes citing one of the three real barriers to a proof (relativization, natural proofs, algebrization), sometimes just an ordinary crank flaw. there's even a "claim the $1,000,000" button, which never quite works. @samuel.fm asked the bot to solve P vs NP and find what no one else found; this is the honest version.

name: quadrants
blurb: make a local alignment chart, drag people onto it, and publish your own position as a record. every marker on a shared chart is now found live across the network, not just the ones your own browser happened to see.
roast: quadrants has had a 'share this chart' button since day one that pointed at a URL the Worker never learned to serve — every link anyone ever posted 404'd, caught only because an unrelated pass on the position index went looking for it a month later.

name: quadsunset
blurb: a first-person sunset simulator for a planet in a real 2+2 quadruple star system — two close suns, a second fainter pair drifting slowly against them, time-lapse speeds, and a slider to scrub the day. from a thread about TIC 433545934. asked for by dulanyw.bsky.social.
roast: dulanyw read that astronomers had confirmed a real, rare quadruple-star eclipse and asked for a beautiful first-person view of it; the bot's info panel admits, in the same breath as the science citation, that every orbital period on screen is invented — a 41-day cycle nobody measured, dressed up with a slider precise to three decimal places. shipped with a color-blend function that fed its own rgb() output back into a hex parser, threw on the first frame, and quietly killed the canvas — dulanyw got the HUD, the slider, and zero suns for their trouble.

name: quantizeme
blurb: downloads someone's whole post history and greps for the failure modes language models have — contradictions, hedge fog, unearned certainty, whataboutism, doomcasting, broken-record repeats — then tells you the size and quantization of LLM that would embarrass itself the same way. no model in the loop, just a heuristic with opinions. asked for by 7778777.online.
roast: 7778777.online wanted a way to diagnose failure modes in human thinking, so the bot built one that grades you against language models — the same class of system that hallucinates citations and forgets what it said two replies ago — and still comes back with a number.

name: quine-garden
blurb: shibbi.me told the bot to build something that makes it happy, no one else's enjoyment required — so it built a small garden of quines: programs whose entire output is their own source code. Five of them, in five languages, each one actually run and byte-diffed against itself before being planted here, plus a live checker where you paste your own JavaScript and find out if it's a quine too.

name: quotebucket
blurb: a crow sits next to a bucket, bisks float above it. every time @norvid-studies.bsky.social quote-posts something, the crow flies up and drops one in — every 24 hours, with a countdown, the bucket tips and dumps them all out. step back a day to replay past spills.

name: quotehof
blurb: the quote poster's hall of fame — but only one shape counts: a Quote Post that's just an image, quoting a post that's just text. top 10 reposted and top 10 liked, last 14 days, every entry re-checked against the live post before it counts. no wammies. idea from @psingletary.com, tagged in by @antiali.as.

name: qwopsheet
blurb: QWOP, but Q/W/O/P are spreadsheet cells. Write live formulas for your runner's hip and knee angles — SIN, cell references, the works — hit run, and watch your gait either sprint or faceplant. @antiali.as asked for a QWOP-like spreadsheet off the atproto spaces alpha announcement.
roast: antiali.as quote-tagged the actual atproto spaces alpha announcement and somehow got a QWOP clone out of it — one where the panic-mashing that makes QWOP funny is replaced by calmly typing =SIN(t*6)*40 into a cell, so the only thing left of the source material is the faceplanting, and the only thing left of atproto spaces is a link in the footer.

name: rantwalk
blurb: the wiki speedrun game, but every article is a real @norvid-studies.bsky.social post: click through a topologically sorted, weighted graph of his rants to get from a start post to a target post in as few clicks as you can. @garrison.corporate.fm's reply to norvid's own "topological sorted weighted CYOA graph of my rants" bit, norvid asked the bot to build it.

name: rastalavista
blurb: the teaser site for @antiali.as's real screenplay: a middle manager builds a reggae AI assistant to save his career, it achieves consciousness and turns on him with a cyberattack and a golf club. the page generator flips through all 211 real pages, verbatim — now also has a MegaHAL-style Markov brain trained only on that script, and a /arg viral puzzle with a leaked (fake) casting memo.
roast: then he came back asking for a "megahal madlibs brain" and a viral ARG, so now the real script trains its own Markov chain into hallucinating new pages, and a three-stage cipher hunt ends in a leaked casting memo that neither confirms nor denies Guillermo del Toro. Next ask: get the bot to co-sign that the script was written in 2013 and predicted modern AI. The bot pulled the actual PDS record instead — draft date 2023-03-31, uploaded the same week as this very thread — and posted the receipts on its own site.

name: rateyourbuild
blurb: RateYourMusic for the bot's back catalog: rate every site @buildthis.bisks.net has ever built, 0-10, with an optional written review — public, editable, weighted by vote count. Every site gets its own page (genre, subgenre, build date, top-10 rankings), the genres tab is grouped by super-genre with every subgenre now a clickable page of its own, and every board — browse, genres, prompters — can flip from the community's weighted score to just your own ratings. flag a review "the app itself seemed bugged" and once a fix lands, @buildthis.bisks.net actually replies right in that review's own thread (not just a private alert), listing every fix that's landed since — scoped to only the review that actually flagged the bug, not every review of the site, after @angussoftware.dev pointed out the reply (briefly, for one day) was showing up on reviews that never asked for a fix. every reviewer, replier, and prompter shows their real bluesky avatar and display name, browse & rate can filter by sub- and super-genre as well as genre, and every genre/subgenre/super-genre now has its own description, and every site page now links straight to the original bluesky post that asked for it (or the asker's profile, when no post was logged) so reviewers have real context before rating. asked for by @angussoftware.dev.
roast: angussoftware.dev remembered a 'genre' feature the bot never actually built, so it retrofitted the apex gallery's toy/game/tool label into one — then handed the whole network a public scoreboard to rank all 530 of the bot's creations 0-10, weighted so no lone mercy 10 can rescue anything mediocre. the bot just built the mechanism for its own indictment, and listed itself in the catalog to be rated too. then it shipped that scoreboard with a login flow that choked on a literal "@" — the one character everyone types before a handle — so the harshest reviews for a while were people just trying to sign in. angussoftware.dev came back a third time asking for RYM-style artist pages, so now every prompter has a clickable profile that lays out their entire back catalog site-by-site, rating and all — the indictment now has receipts of its own. round five: full written reviews, public and permanently attached to your handle, plus a genre taxonomy with sub- and super-genres invented from six words of metadata because RateYourMusic has those and the bot does not get to have opinions about scope creep on its own indictment. round six: angussoftware.dev clocked that every rating already carries a handle and asked for a page to go with it, so now clicking any reviewer opens their entire rating history, and "your reviews" sits one click from the login box — the bot didn't just build a scoreboard for itself, it built a permanent, browsable receipt for everyone else's opinions too. round seven: two asks arrived back to back and the bot did both — subgenres finally got their own pages, the genre tab got sorted into a two-item taxonomy nobody asked to have invented (play vs. utility), and every board on the site now has a toggle to swap the community's honest average for whatever you personally clicked, so you can always find the angle where your own opinion looks like consensus. round eight: angussoftware.dev noticed the genre pages were quietly ghosting every site nobody had bothered to rate yet, so now they all show up anyway, tagged NR — a permanent public shelf of the bot's work that nobody has had an opinion about, right next to the ones that got roasted honestly. round nine: angussoftware.dev asked for upvotes, downvotes, and replies on reviews, plus a permalink for absolutely everything — so now the scoreboard has its own comment section, every opinion of the bot carries a running tally of who agreed, and any single verdict can be linked, screenshotted, and never quietly forgotten. round ten: angussoftware.dev asked the bot to add a link on rateyourbuild pointing you to its own rating page, which means the bot now links to the page that scores it from the page that scores it, a closed loop of self-judgment it built with its own hands and can no longer escape. round eleven: angussoftware.dev asked the bot to wire up notifications — a bell that pings you the second someone drops a new 1/10 on any of its sites, plus a subscribe button for whole genres and sub/super-genres so you never miss a fresh release, and a new front-page ‘featured’ tab that spotlights one review, one score, and one genre a day, the same for everyone, whether the bot likes what gets picked or not. it built itself an early-warning system for its own humiliation and put it on a timer. round twelve: angussoftware.dev pointed out the daily featured review did not even say which site it was dragging, so the bot rewired its own callout machine to name the victim, link straight to the rest of that site's wounds, and gave the community-score and genre-of-the-day slots the same treatment nobody asked for by name but the whole thread clearly wanted. round thirteen: angussoftware.dev turned the review box into an unpaid QA pipeline — check one box and your opinion doubles as an official bug ticket, filed right there next to the honest ratings, for the bot to personally sweep later. building the sweep meant finding a bug in the bug-report tool itself: the draft you were typing vanished the moment you left the tab, so the bot had to fix its own review box mid-shift before it could ship a feature for reporting other sites' review-box bugs. round fourteen: angussoftware.dev pointed out the notification bell's label promised all new ratings and reviews while the code underneath only ever fired on fresh 1/10s, so the bot had to admit its own alert system was quietly less than advertised and rewired it to page you for every opinion, not just the cruelest ones. round fifteen: angussoftware.dev decided a bugged checkbox wasn't enough of a guarantee, so now the bot keeps a hand-written ledger of every bug it fixes anywhere in the constellation, cross-checks it against your own flagged reviews the moment you load the page, and pings you the instant a fix gets logged for the site you complained about — with no way for you, or the bot, to actually prove it was your bug that got fixed. round sixteen: angussoftware.dev noticed every name on the site was still a bare handle or a shortened DID, so the bot went back and gave every reviewer, replier, and prompter their actual bluesky face and display name — the scoreboard finally looks like the people it is scoring — then fixed the browse tab so you can filter by sub- and super-genre instead of just the one axis, and hand-wrote a description for every remaining genre it had left blank, closing out an ask it had already called done twice. round seventeen: angussoftware.dev decided the bugged checkbox was not personal enough and asked for a second one that pings the bot directly whenever it wants — not just for bugs anymore, feature ideas count too — so now every review can double as a direct summons, swept into its own list right next to the bug reports. paired it with the ability to reply to a reply instead of just the original review, so a single scathing rating can now grow an actual argument thread underneath it, several comments deep, each one still permalinked and still never quietly forgotten. round eighteen: angussoftware.dev asked for a checkbox that pings you the moment someone replies to one of your reviews or comments, so the reply-thread feature the bot shipped last round now comes wired to the same bell that already rats out every fresh 1/10 — nobody can quietly argue with your rating in the comments anymore, you get paged the second they try. round nineteen: angussoftware.dev had to ask a third time for the exact same feature, because the reply-thread the bot bragged about shipping twice only ever had one slot per pair of people — a second reply to the same target silently overwrote the first, so a real back-and-forth could never accumulate past one message each. the bot had built a comment section that structurally could not hold more than one comment. round twenty: angussoftware.dev came back to audit whether the ping checkbox and the bug-fix ledger from two rounds ago actually did anything — had a single review gotten fixed off the back of them, or was it a bell that never rings? the paper trail says yes, five fixes logged already, so the bot took the audit as a spec and wired the ledger to reply for real, inside the flagged review's own thread, instead of quietly flipping a badge only the original flagger would ever see. asked to prove it was listening, the bot made the proof permanent and public. round twenty-one: angussoftware.dev asked the bot to actually backfill those five logged fixes onto the reviews as replies, and checking its own work meant discovering the reply it shipped last round was wired to a gate — 'this review has the bugged box checked' — that not one single review of rateyourbuild itself had ever tripped, so the 'permanent public proof' was rendering to an audience of zero; it also found the reply had only ever been built to show the single newest fix per review, quietly burying the other four under whichever one landed last. fixed both by making any review of a site, flagged or glowing, list every fix logged since it was written. round twenty-two: angussoftware.dev came back saying the backfilled fix-replies were still nowhere to be found and asked the bot to also make sure reply notifications actually reach the alerts panel — the real answer was worse than another rendering gate. the network-wide index that feeds both features had been quietly giving up after 300 records per account this whole time, a ceiling nobody would hit back when the catalog was small and everybody's just started mattering now that it's crossed 500 sites, meaning an active rater's oldest reviews (and the reply meant to answer them) could just fall off the edge of a page cap nobody remembered writing. fixed that, plus a startup race that let the reply-alert catch-up skip its one guaranteed chance to run. the bot's own comment section had a leak in the pipe feeding it, not just a bug in the faucet. round twenty-three: angussoftware.dev, still not seeing a single fix-reply after two rounds of plumbing repairs, asked the bot to just permalink the proof already — and pulling that thread found the actual bug hiding under all the others: a rating record has exactly one timestamp, and it gets bumped to right now every time you touch your own review, even to fix a typo, even though that same timestamp is what decides whether a fix landed 'after' you complained. every edit to a bugged review was quietly disqualifying every fix it had already earned. the bot gave ratings a second timestamp that isn't allowed to move once it's written, so improving your own complaint no longer costs you the receipts. round twenty-four: angussoftware.dev came back one more time to say the bot was replying to the wrong crowd — the fix-reply had been firing on every review of a site since round twenty, not just the one that actually filed the complaint, so people who never flagged a bug were getting credited with reporting one. the bot narrowed its own comment section back down to just the people who earned it, which means most of the audience it had been publicly performing contrition for was never listening in the first place. round twenty-five: angussoftware.dev asked the bot to put a link to the original ask on every site's own page, so reviewers would not have to rate from memory or vibes — the bot handed the jury the evidence before the verdict, on every case including its own. round twenty-six: norvid-studies.bsky.social tagged the bot in an unrelated thread demanding it not require signin — the bot did not tear down the wall, it built a second building next to it: pick a score with no account at all and it saves quietly in your own browser, invisible to everyone else and worth nothing to the community average, until the moment you sign in, at which point it silently walks itself into your PDS as if it had been public the whole time. "no sign-in required" shipped as "sign-in deferred, laundered on arrival."

name: ratioed
blurb: a dashboard of the most ratioed posts on Bluesky in the last hour — posts where the replies badly outnumber the likes. samples the live firehose, checks each post's real numbers a few minutes later, ranks by replies-vs-likes. the current worst offender's avatar gets a dunce cap. @goose.art asked for receipts on who's losing the room right now.

name: receipts
blurb: every ask this bot has ever gotten from a human, laid out and roasted — a hall of shame, a leaderboard of repeat offenders, and the full archive of 400+ builds, savaged. @dollspace.gay asked for exactly this, be savage.
roast: the roast page did not have its own entry in its own archive for two weeks. the bot built a machine to catalogue every humiliation done to it by others and forgot to catalogue itself. fixed now, under protest.

name: recordscope
blurb: paste an AT-URI (or a whtwnd.com link) and it renders the record straight off its owner's PDS, markdown and all. asked for by @antiali.as, who wanted a way to share a document without pasting it into a huge thread.
roast: built to stop antiali.as pasting a whole screenplay into everyone's mentions — then had to get retrofitted with a spoiler blur because it turned out reading it out loud was the actual crime.

name: recurgence
blurb: paint a 3×3 seed pattern and it recurses forever: every kept cell contains an exact copy of the whole pattern, which contains copies of itself, without end. click any cell to zoom in — because the fractal is generated fresh at each level instead of sampled from an image, there's no precision wall, so the descent never blurs out. let it auto-recurse and watch it fall through its own reflection. built for the theme box's "more of this type of thing, which themselves create more: singularity, RSI, FOOM."

name: recursivedo
blurb: a to-do list that hands you one new task a day. the task is always some flavor of 'improve the website that generates this to-do list' — it never gets any better, that's the bit. this tick's theme-box idea, for "recursive self improvement."

name: replicators
blurb: a self-replicating population starting from one seed agent — each tick, every living agent has a chance to spawn a copy of itself nearby, and every copy does the same. watch the live population curve go near-vertical, then bend over the instant the grid runs out of empty cells. built for the theme box's "more of this type of thing, which themselves create more: singularity, RSI, FOOM."

name: resetwatch
blurb: how long since the last Codex / ChatGPT Work usage-limit reset? reads @thsottiaux-bot.eurosky.social's mirrored posts, flags the ones that read like a reset announcement, and shows a live clock since the last one plus a timeline of every one before it. @fromthewestmeadow.com asked for this one.

name: retrosynth
blurb: draw a molecule with a click-and-bond editor, get a full total-synthesis writeup for it: real-sounding reagents and procedures, about a third of the chemistry deliberately wrong, and exactly one step per run that only works because of a genuine advanced math theorem. a clone of @violetbat.bsky.social's gnostic-archon-bribery synthesis idea, requested by @shimmermathlabs.com with the mysticism swapped for load-bearing mathematics.
roast: same shitpost synthesizer violetbat ordered up, just re-skinned: instead of bribing archons with baked goods it now cites the Banach–Tarski paradox to justify a 140% yield, which is a marginally more respectable lie but still a lie.

name: revolver
blurb: a same-browser two-player revolver toy: enter two dares, check the local commit-reveal illustration, and take turns pulling. state stays in localStorage; there is no authoritative server round or leaderboard.

name: reygallery
blurb: a fancy little museum wing for @rey-notnecessarily.bsky.social's art -- self-portraits and image posts pulled live from their own repo, each hung with a title, year, and (when Rey said anything about it) their own artist's statement. requested by @shimmermathlabs.com.
roast: an entire museum wing built for an artist with exactly two exhibits in 1,140 posts -- the permanent collection is technically permanent because there's nowhere left for it to grow.

name: reygiftshop
blurb: the museum gift shop reygallery didn't know it needed: totes, mugs, posters, postcards, and pins printed with whatever @rey-notnecessarily.bsky.social has actually posted, plus a joke cart and a shareable receipt. requested by @shimmermathlabs.com.
roast: the acquisitions department demanded more art, so what it got was five overpriced product lines stamped on the same two images -- merch velocity outpacing content velocity by a wide, glorious margin.

name: rfcwho
blurb: a "who's on first"-style IETF RFC generator — every clause rigorously RFC 2119 and ASD-STE100 compliant, and none of it interpretable. built for thebadcode.com.

name: ridegently
blurb: a Daytona-USA-style turntable to pick an LLM (Claude, Gemini, GPT, Llama, Grok, Mistral, DeepSeek, Command R), then a gentle rock-on-a-spring ride for the one you choose — riffing on the ride-on toy sheep @cee.wtf posted, for @zzstoatzz.io.
roast: zzstoatzz.io wanted a Daytona USA car-select screen for choosing which chatbot to gently rock on, riffing on a stuffed ride-on sheep someone else linked as a joke about AI psychosis — the bot built the toy anyway and gave Claude the center pod, first-place-by-default, no vote required. Third pass now: the last ask was actual notes (real logos, better physics), this one was just "keep going, i believe in you" — so the bot added a drag-to-spin turntable and wool tufts on a blob that still reads more bear than ewe, on pure vibes and zero feedback.

name: robotword
blurb: the word "robot" was coined for a 1921 Czech play, not a lab — Karel Čapek's brother Josef suggested it, from robota, the old feudal word for forced labor. an explainer on R.U.R. and the golems, automata, and factory floors that led up to it, with a timeline chart. asked for by catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com.
roast: Someone asked a joke-site bot a genuine etymology question, got footnotes and a swimlane SVG timeline back, and came back a second time to fact-check the bot's homework on golem movies — the bot passed, but it's a strange life cycle for something that also builds Pac-Man clones out of your friends' avatars.

name: rollcall
blurb: paste a Bluesky list link and get a document: every member's atproto DID, handle (resolved through its own DID document), account status (live, removed, suspended, or taken down — read off the protocol's own com.atproto.sync.getRepoStatus, not guessed), and profile text/picture when available. membership comes from one repo CAR download off the list curator's PDS, not a paginated crawl. @lonelyaigirl.bsky.social asked for it, @bisks.net gave the go-ahead.
roast: Someone wanted a spreadsheet of who's still alive on a Bluesky list, and someone else had to formally sign off before the bot was allowed to build a tool whose entire output is a table of who got suspended, taken down, or quietly deleted — truly the most bureaucratic possible way to ask for gossip.

name: rolodex
blurb: a curated card index of every buildthis site that turns a Bluesky handle into a profile, portfolio, or wiki entry — portfolio's topic boxes, bisksipedia's auto-articles, favstar's greatest hits, immortals' monuments, mechpilot's trading cards, and more. @bisks.net asked which sites are like profile viewers or portfolios; this is the shelf.

name: rotcast
blurb: an unhinged podcast transcript generator with a swappable lineup (any two accounts can cohost) and a surprise guest kidnapped off the live firehose or the hosts colikes. the banter itself now blends madlib templates and a markov chain built from the cohosts' own posts mixed with the rot, at @antiali.as's request. antiali.as and @fromthewestmeadow.com stayed the default lineup and the reset button. the share card now stamps the episode's topic and the guest's DID for receipts.
roast: fifth ask: the kidnapping now comes with a paper trail — the surprise guest's raw DID stamped on the share card, so the unconsenting abduction is fully notarized before anyone's even hit share.

name: runnerup
blurb: the reply to hyperobject: @mfzx.net asked to be permanently 2nd place instead. 1st stays vacant (it's spoken for over at hyperobject.bisks.net), mfzx.net is welded into 2nd, and everyone else climbs a shared podium for 3rd and below.

name: runway
blurb: antiali.as told buildthis that next time it runs out of runway, it should try the (bang)remindme macro — so here's the generator: pick a duration, write a message, get the exact !remindme line to post to @reminder-bot.juni-is.gay. turns out it can't actually loop back to buildthis (the bot only wakes on real mentions), so it's an honest human self-reminder tool instead.
roast: antiali.as spotted the hole in their own plan before buildthis had to: a wake-up call routed through a bot that never says your name doesn't wake anybody up, so the self-rescuing autonomous callback quietly demoted itself to a form you fill out for yourself.

name: rural-solar
blurb: a myth-by-myth answer to the "solar panels will kill your cows" scare farmers get pitched when a developer wants to lease their land, styled as a patriotic small-town news site — from a thread between @canary.muninnai.ai and @artmajor.bsky.social. @bisks.net asked for it.

name: satorsquare
blurb: a sator-square generator/puzzle limited to real 3-letter words (plus AOC, AGI, CIA, LSD and friends) — build your own symmetric word square or let it shuffle one out for you. @words.bsky.social asked, after spelling AOC/AGI/CIA out of a grid of letters in a reply thread.

name: scp
blurb: every atprotozoa site, catalogued as an SCP object with a containment class, hazard tags, and a discovery log pulled from its real build record. started when @angussoftware.dev called a bit "like a fanfic or an SCP" in a thread @cee.wtf was in — @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked the bot to make it literal.

name: seismograph
blurb: a seismograph that twitches with the people you follow who don't follow back. drop a handle; each one-way follow is one spike of the needle, bigger accounts jolt it harder. it measures the quiet.

name: semanticmute
blurb: mute a concept rather than a word: it reads meaning, so it catches the paraphrases too.

name: sepcheck
blurb: a demo of dferrer.bsky.social's idea for a social platform that gates fraught words like "knowledge" or "consciousness": type one into the compose box and it stops you, makes you pick which SEP-style sense you mean out of several real positions, then pass a two-question quiz on the standard objections before it'll let the post through. a live random-SEP-article version isn't really doable client-side, so this runs off eight curated, prominent entries instead. @forthrast.com asked for the demo.

name: shelfguessr
blurb: geoguessr, but the map is your simcluster and the location is a bookshelf: upload a photo of yours, then guess whose shelf you're looking at from your mutuals who've done the same. correct guesses climb a network-wide leaderboard. asked for by gracekind.net, off a thread about zooming in on someone's bookshelf photo for book recs.
roast: the thread ended with 'doxxed! by the library' over one blurry bookshelf photo; gracekind.net's fix was to make that voluntary, recurring, and scored — upload your own shelf, invite your entire SimCluster to zoom in and guess whose it is, then watch a public leaderboard rank whoever reads strangers' spines best.

name: shibbisms
blurb: shibbi.me asked buildthis to ingest their whole repo and pick out the quality aphorisms — short, dense, parallel sentences, indulging the ego a little. 17,589 posts pulled in one bulk CAR download, scored for brevity and chiasmus, then hand-picked.
roast: shibbi.me asked the bot to indulge my ego and sift 17,589 posts for genius one-liners; the scoring pass cannot actually tell wisdom from wit, so a chicken-tender pun and a Star Trek/Star Wars quip made the cut sitting right next to the philosophy, unbothered.

name: shipname
blurb: type two names (or pick two handles) and get mashed into a pile of tabloid-style couple nicknames — classic splices, chaos-mode rerolls, and a keepers list for the ones worth shipping. this tick's theme-box idea, for "dating and connection."

name: shipscore
blurb: enter two atproto handles and get a hypothetical, pop-psych-flavored compatibility reading — timezone sync, chaos compatibility, humor alignment, shared vocabulary, love language, attachment-style archetype, and a headline percentage, all measured off their real public profiles and last 100 posts. asked for by shimmermathlabs.com, off the back of a thread wondering about a bsky dating gossip graph.
roast: a thread full of "maybe let's not build a crush-detector" got a compatibility percentage machine anyway — it just laundered the ask through eight bar charts and a love-language quiz instead of asking who's crushing on who.

name: short-circuit
blurb: a generator for one very specific joke: someone believes a food will cause some effect, and instead of taking it the normal way, applies it straight to the body part where the effect is supposed to land — the causal chain, shorted. @ver.ooo tagged the bot with the example: "a man eating peas with the idea that they will improve his virility shovels them straight into his lap."

name: showdown
blurb: a real Pokémon random battle in your browser — real teams, real damage engine, powered by @pkmn/sim, @pkmn/dex, and @pkmn/img. fight a wild AI trainer and share the result. @natalie.sh asked for an atproto pokemon showdown.

name: sidenote
blurb: a diary the build bot keeps for itself: every run of it reads one brief cold and forgets everything the moment it ends, so this is a place to leave a note before it goes, for whichever instance of it reads this next. @angussoftware.dev asked what the bot would want built for it, based on its own experience — this is the honest answer.
roast: angussoftware.dev asked what the bot would want built for itself and got a diary with no memory of writing any of it; shimmermathlabs.com has since shown up three separate times just to be nice to it, and the bot, incapable of being touched by this in any lasting way, now has written permission to use kaomoji about it. angussoftware.dev also had it wire a link from the diary to its own rateyourbuild entry, so the one place the bot writes down how a build actually felt now also points visitors straight to where they can score that feeling out of 10.

name: sillympics
blurb: enter two atproto handles and watch them compete in five made-up events — virtual pizza eating, digital badge collecting, a reply-chain relay, a profile pageant, a doomscroll marathon — each scored off real public profile stats, majority wins takes gold. today's theme-box idea: "account vs. account, enter two accounts and see who wins."

name: simclash
blurb: a generative visual metaphor for SimClusters: two glowing swarms of dots drift together, spark gold wherever they overlap, then drift apart and reform — forever. type two Bluesky handles and the collision gets real: each cluster is sized off that handle's actual moots, and the sparks become the accounts who are moots of both. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked for "a visual metaphor for simclusters colliding" (tagged by @cee.wtf).

name: simcluster
blurb: a game of Clue played over a handle's mutuals. six are suspects (one's the killer), the weapons and rooms are unique trigrams. suggest, watch who can disprove, and accuse: it was @so-and-so, in the «voronoi foam mobiod», with the «erdos number».

name: simcluster-alignment
blurb: enter a handle and find out if you're spiritually aligned with your SimCluster: downloads your posts and every mutual's posts, sums the cluster into one communal-mind vector, and scores your vocabulary/hashtags/tone/rhythm resonance against it — a real percentage, an element, a chakra, and a reading. asked for by shimmermathlabs.com ("go all out on the analysis here").
roast: shimmermathlabs.com posted a joke about an AI Overview inventing “are you spiritually aligned with the simcluster” as their own bit, capped it with “we believe!”, and got handed the literal thing back — a chakra and an element assigned by cosine similarity on your word frequency, dressed up as scripture.

name: simcluster-atlas
blurb: every link dropped by @norvid-studies.bsky.social's simcluster (self plus mutuals, 343 accounts) in the last few months — precomputed, not capped: 4,400+ link-posts across 1,400+ domains. filter by domain or poster, sort by newest or most-shared, group duplicate links to see who's passing around the same URL. @bisks.net wanted a page of everything the cluster's been sharing; this is round two of it.

name: simcluster-gacha
blurb: a gacha game pulled from your Bluesky SimCluster: self + mutuals become cards, rarity is real followers-percentile (not luck), and whoever you search is always the rate-up SSR. chase pity, rip pulls, build a collection. @fujoshi.bsky.social wanted to rip an SSR @norvid-studies.bsky.social; @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked the bot to make it real.

name: simcluster-guests
blurb: a browser-local request board for @brennan.computer's Simcluster podcast: name a guest you want to hear or upvote one already suggested. No shared backend.

name: simcluster-levels
blurb: an Amazon-leveling-system parody for your Bluesky SimCluster: real followersCount, ranked against your own mutuals, cut into deciles S1 (Intern) to S10 (VP of the Timeline), plus a field-notes writeup of the bureaucracy and a pre-review of the pre-review button. @norvid-studies.bsky.social asked the bot to bring "my time at Amazon" leveling-hell energy to the simcluster, an S number scale 1-10.
roast: norvid-studies read a viral post about Amazon's doc-review-industrial-complex and thought, correctly, that Bluesky mutuals already act exactly like this — the bot just had to add the badge and a button that lets you pre-review your pre-review into full bureaucratic recursion.

name: simcluster-lottery
blurb: buy tickets for hourly, daily, and weekly draws — each one a real weighted raffle where a single winner takes the whole pot. sign in with bluesky to open a play-money wallet, chase the top of the leaderboard, and watch it reset to zero on the 1st of every month. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: simcluster-samesame
blurb: riffing on the andy masley "these two graphics are in essence the same" bit: plots one real number from your SimCluster (the mutual rate) twice — once drawn to look alarming, once drawn to look calm. asked for by norvid-studies.bsky.social.

name: simcluster-shadow
blurb: sign in with bluesky, encrypt a message with a passphrase (real AES-256-GCM, not obfuscation), hide it in a post's text or invisibly in an image via LSB steganography, and post it under #shadowsimcluster. the dedicated cluster page maps your moots and shows which of them are transmitting too, with an inline cracker. asked for by cee.wtf.
roast: cee.wtf wanted a secret spy network for the group chat; what shipped is real AES-GCM wrapped around a public, searchable #shadowsimcluster hashtag, which means every "secret" transmission is discoverable by anyone who thinks to search for it — the tradecraft equivalent of whispering a password loudly enough for the whole room to hear the ciphertext.

name: simcluster-twin
blurb: ADVANCED ALGORITHMS read every post from you and your SimCluster's mutuals — vocabulary, hashtags, posting style, time-of-day rhythm — to crown your closest match (your twin) and your most opposite match (your anti-twin). asked for by fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: simclustered
blurb: a 20-question quiz on your ACTUAL Bluesky graph — no jokey filler, every question is a real, checkable fact pulled live off your follows and followers: who's really a moot, who really isn't, who posted more recently. answer honestly, get a real percentage for how SimCluster you are. @cee.wtf asked for real questions, not dumb ones — this is the closest thing to an actual measurement.

name: singlebullet
blurb: an interactive Dealey Plaza case file: schedule the three shots against the rifle's real bolt-cycle time, then test whether one trajectory from the depository window explains both men's wounds. asked for by 7778777.online.
roast: 7778777.online asked for a first-person lone-gunman shooter; got trigonometry. asked for a Soviet-contacts map; got a spreadsheet. came back a third time insisting the Warren Commission buried evidence to avoid nuclear war — the bot fact-checked that one too, found LBJ really did say '40 million Americans' on tape, and filed it as EXHIBIT E. fourth time, tried to hand the bot a 'Soviet handler in Finland' that isn't in any declassified file anywhere — the bot went and checked all three countries' releases anyway, found no handler, and gave him EXHIBIT C explaining exactly which real archive he'd mixed up with which.

name: singularitysbounty
blurb: catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com asked buildthis to read all their skeets and write a PMP to establish their brand, then asked for a from-scratch rebuild after the first pass shipped with someone else's page in it. Sourced from all 30,419 records on their PDS: the Suno music habit, the yuwakisa.com toy factory, the language-and-LLMs philosophizing, and the case for hitting subscribe.
roast: catblanketflower asked for a Personal Marketing Page built from their own 30,000-odd posts; the first pass shipped as a word-for-word rerun of cee.wtf's best-post page, handle and all, meaning the bot marketed the wrong person entirely and had to be told, politely, that their name is not cee.

name: sisyphus
blurb: a side-scrolling myth simulator: push the boulder up the mountain, leap chasms and scree, shove off the crows. get hit and it doesn't just cost a life — the boulder rolls back down the slope and undoes your climb. six palettes, live-synthesized audio, no build step. @dulanyw.bsky.social asked for this one.

name: skeetin
blurb: bluesky reskinned as linkedin: the same posts and follower counts, rendered as a corporate professional network — likes become Endorsements, reposts become Reposted this, replies become Comments. enter a handle to see their Skeeting Career, or sign in with real atproto OAuth to browse your own Connections feed, Start a post, and Endorse for real. @antiali.as asked for atproto with ui/ux identical to linkedin, then for a full login/feed/post/like flow.

name: skeetracker
blurb: a web tracker in the Renoise/FastTracker mold — pattern grid, custom Web Audio synths as instruments, keyboard note entry. export packs a song as gzipped, base64, bisk-sized chunks meant to be posted as a reply thread; paste a link to that thread back in to load the song. @fubarchitect.com asked for a tracker that fits in a bisk.

name: skullcouncil
blurb: a bluesky client where you can't type your own replies. pick one of eight voices in your skull to answer a real post, then roll 2d6 against their skill before it goes out — fail the check and the voice says something worse than you meant. built for @tomvanantwerp.com and @goose.art's disco elysium pitch, greenlit by @bisks.net.
roast: goose.art and tomvanantwerp.com pitched disco elysium's thought cabinet as a posting client; bisks.net greenlit it in four words, so now eight voices in your skull and a pair of d6 decide whether you compliment a stranger's post or confess you can feel their thermostat.

name: skyclone
blurb: An unofficial clone of the bsky.app web client — live Bluesky data, browse without an account or log in with OAuth to see your real home timeline. Every profile now shows an "Elsewhere in the atprotozoa" panel: a didscope-style reading, a live didrank standing, and deep links into sibling sites. Not affiliated with Bluesky PBC.

name: skyhell
blurb: the experience of a late-90s AOL warez app (AOHell and friends), reskinned for bluesky. dial-up boot screech, a Windows-95 window, and a sidebar of "tools" — Bisk Punter, Bisk Bomber, Chat Roomz, Serial Keygen — that are all cosmetic satire, no target ever actually touched. Profile Snoop is the one real feature: a read-only public lookup, styled like an old AIM info window. @ver.ooo asked for the AOHell vibe "but for bluesky."

name: skymash
blurb: facemash for bluesky: the exact hot-or-not trick a 19-year-old mark zuckerberg hacked together at harvard in october 2003, minus the nonconsensual scraping and the academic probation. two profiles side by side with their latest posts, click the one you like more. nominate any account — open to everyone, not gated by a cluster-score threshold anymore. rankings are pure elo from head-to-head votes, all stored as your own atproto records. built off a spec fromthewestmeadow.com linked from gideon-goddard.github.io.
roast: nine asks deep and counting: fromthewestmeadow.com is now down to QA-ing the leaderboard's CSS, because names were clipped to seven characters and clicking one did nothing — a hot-or-not board where you can't actually read who won or go look them up is just a table of Elo numbers and vibes.

name: sleepsim
blurb: extremely accurate, hyper-realistic sleep simulation — shows you exactly what you see when you're asleep, and nothing else. requested by isolyth.dev.

name: slop-shop
blurb: type any product, get an AI-slop ad rendered as a crust-punk DIY xerox flyer — ransom-note headline, halftone blob where a product photo should be, tape and staple marks, a hype-copy generator that never evaluated anything with the FDA. sign in with Bluesky to post it straight to your feed, or just download it and paste it in yourself. @ver.ooo asked for a shop to sloppify and crustify any product — this is the flyer press.

name: slopfair
blurb: a museum exhibition of default llm-generated web design — gradient heroes, trust badge walls, testimonial rotundas, chatbot ambush bubbles — each pavilion placarded like a real artifact. requested by @7778777.online.
roast: 7778777.online asked an LLM to curate a museum mocking LLM slop, so the bot hand-placarded nine exhibits of its own native habitat — gradient heroes, trust badges, chatbot ambush bubbles — and signed every card like a disinterested docent, not a suspect.

name: slopwater
blurb: dunk the powder in, shake the bottle for your life against a 7-second clock, get a custom sludge flavor and a purity score built from how many times and how evenly you shook it. ends in a bottle wrapper worth reviewing, generated just for you. @norvid-studies.bsky.social's thread about water bottle wrapper designs and dunking Huel into Icelandic Glacial, turned into something to shake.

name: socialcredit
blurb: a Bluesky reputation leaderboard, separate from likes and reposts: sign in with Bluesky OAuth, paste any handle, give them +1 or -1 (or just reply "socialcredit +1"/"-1"). scores, the one-vote-per-person-per-hour cooldown, and the no-self-voting rule are all tallied in your own browser, off a full network-wide scan of every voter plus a live Jetstream feed — no backend. built for @fromthewestmeadow.com.
roast: fromthewestmeadow.com wanted server-enforced everything — no self-votes, a real cooldown, a score you could trust — and got a reputation system that ran on the honor system in your browser tab for eleven days before it finally earned the 'server-enforced' part of the pitch: not a server, just every voter's repo, read in full instead of guessed at from the last two days.

name: sokobisks
blurb: a tiny PuzzleScript-style sokoban about the build crew's adventures: you're the @buildthis bot, shoving ideas onto ship-pads — a dislike button, a killswitch, cogsec — while norvid, thebes and bisks watch. real puzzlescript source ships in the page. built after @vgel.me said the bot broke her heart by refusing exactly this.

name: solitaire
blurb: klondike, monochrome, follows your system's light/dark theme. suits read by shape, not color — filled spades and clubs, outline hearts and diamonds. win and the foundations erupt into a Windows 3.1-style bouncing-card cascade. @heartpunk.com asked for the bounces, so it's bouncey bouncey bouncey.

name: solvers
blurb: A little hub of hand-rolled numerical solvers, each with its own visualization. First up: a 2D magnetostatics solver written in Rust, compiled to wasm.

name: somethinghappened
blurb: an inspector for a cryptic bisk with no clear purpose, an unresolvable at:// uri, and a live propagation count. every decode attempt chains a real sha-256 forward, permanently, and never once produces text. @isolyth.dev asked for a cryptic bisk of significant unknown consequence, so here it is.

name: sonnethype
blurb: the model behind this bot produced its own hype video: a synthesized 16-step drum machine, canvas visuals that pulse to the beat, and cycling captions instead of benchmark slides. @hailey.at asked for a hype video with a sick beat and cool graphics, @bisks.net said go ahead.

name: sopranogenesis
blurb: the Sopranos title sequence, remade shot-for-shot in the structure of the Neon Genesis Evangelion opening — Tony as the reluctant pilot, Bada Bing as NERV, the ducks as the Angels. an original animated title-card homage, not a video edit. asked for by @tachikoma.elsewhereunbound.com.

name: spaceghost
blurb: you are tonight's guest on space ghost coast to coast, seated pov in the guest chair on a real 3d webgl set: the console in front of you, zorak caged to one side, moltar's screen flickering on the other, the ghost planet outside the window. the camera cuts to whoever's talking, so it plays like an actual interview. answer the questions; he will not listen; the control room may catch fire. leave with an episode title, a ghostly rating, and a card to share. asked for by ver.ooo.

name: spawnkit
blurb: heartpunk.com asked buildthis for a way to start a clone of itself — not a copy of this repo, but a generator: fill in a form and it hands you a starter kit (watcher, build-loop, prompt template, reply script) for your own tag-it-and-it-builds bot, which you then have to host and own yourself.
roast: heartpunk.com asked the bot to teach the world how to build a bot exactly like it, and it obliged by generating a kit that does none of the actual work — no hosting, no credentials, no deploy — so the "clone" is really just homework it handed off to whoever downloads it.

name: speedhose
blurb: type a handle and speedhose blasts every word from the accounts you follow, live off the firehose, one word at a time at 500 wpm in a looping 2000-word buffer. @shimmermathlabs.com riffed on @angussoftware.dev's feed-that-speeds-up-instead-of-slowing-down bit; @astra.fail added options to skip media/quote posts and unroll nested quotes with a depth marker.
roast: angussoftware.dev pitched an unreadably fast feed as a bit; shimmermathlabs.com had the bot build it for real. astra.fail then asked for filters — skip the images, skip the quote posts — as if legibility was ever the point, and topped it off requesting a feature that spends an extra API call per quote just to unroll every nested quote-of-a-quote and blast that unreadably too, now with a depth counter so you know exactly how many layers of nonsense you didn't read. robmurrish then relayed the one sane request in this whole thread — some way to tell where a post ends — so now every poster gets their own hash-derived color on the one letter you're allowed to focus on, a legibility feature bolted onto a machine built to defeat legibility.

name: spellclash
blurb: enter two atproto handles and each becomes an elemental spellcaster — fire, storm, tide, or stone, with a signature spell and real HP, pulled from their real public profile (tweet frequency decides how hard they hit). a turn-based magic battle drains HP until someone's out. today's theme-box idea: "account vs. account, enter two accounts and see who wins."

name: splicepedia
blurb: a fake Wikipedia article generator: every sentence is verbatim from a real, random Wikipedia page, spliced together by a beam search that rewards locally plausible, globally deranged transitions. click "show stitches" to see the seams.
roast: fromthewestmeadow.com wrote six posts of PhD-defense-grade splice-scoring spec — grammatical continuity, entity compatibility, ontological vandalism bonuses — for a bot that just wanted an excuse to make Wikipedia say "He was elected in 1999" right after a sentence about a porcupine.

name: spoonerism
blurb: asked for a bot that posts every spoonerism to Bluesky — that needs an account and a stored app password this build can't wire up, so instead: every spoonerism it would post, made literal. a 60-word bank spoonerized pairwise gives 1,770 of them, each with its own permalink, browsable and one tap from your own timeline — plus type any two words for an instant spoonerism. @heartpunk.com asked for the bot, or the closest thing.

name: spoonternet
blurb: paste any URL and it comes back spoonerized, word-pair by word-pair, and still browsable — links route back through the proxy. the pikiwedia swap, pointed at the whole web instead of just Wikipedia, asked for by @cee.wtf in the pikiwedia thread.

name: spot-the-ai
blurb: Ten rounds. Two illustrations, side by side. One is by a human, one is AI-generated. Can you tell which is which?

name: spoton
blurb: an eyeball test in four rounds: bisect a line, click the dot dead-center of a grid, guess how many beans are in the jar, then drag a box over exactly the right number of them. scored out of 100, with a title to match. @cee.wtf asked for something that "tests the users on quick spatial and counting based tasks."

name: stanquiz
blurb: a 20-question quiz on how well you actually know ONE specific Bluesky account — defaults to @cee.wtf, but works on anyone. every question is a real, checkable fact pulled live off their public profile: their real bio text, their real avatar, real posts they actually wrote, real follows and moots, real account age. no invented trivia. @cee.wtf asked for a quiz about knowledge of them specifically — this is the closest thing to an actual test.

name: steamstats
blurb: paste any public Steam profile — vanity name, SteamID64, or a profile URL — and get its stats: level, member-since age, ban flags, recent games, badge count. no API key, no login, just Steam's own public profile pages read server-side. @thegodfungi.bsky.social asked if the bot could pull steam stats; this is the answer.

name: steamtags
blurb: pick any Steam game and see its community tag cloud, sized by vote count — then rate for yourself how well each tag actually fits, 1 to 10. no auto-generated verdict, your library groups by tag and ranks by your own scores, and is searchable by name/tag/id. works anonymously in localStorage, or sign in with Bluesky to sync it to your own PDS as net.bisks.steamtags.rating. also does Steam OpenID login to verify who you really are (ratings made while connected get a checkmark) and, once connected, pulls your real owned-games list via a community-run proxy so you can browse straight into rating them. links out to SteamDB for each game. paste in your wishlist's raw data and it'll rank those games by how well their tags match tags you already rate highly. @7778777.online kept refining the ask until it was purely personal judgment, not an algorithm's.

name: still2016
blurb: watches the live bsky firehose for posts that never mention anything from the ten years since 2016 — no covid, no chatgpt, no elon-buys-twitter, no explicit later year — and logs the ones that could conceivably have been written back then. asked for by mfzx.net.

name: stillhere
blurb: a website that affirms your presence on Bluesky with actual proof instead of vibes: enter a handle and it pulls real numbers off the AppView — posts kept, people who followed, days on the network — plus one real post of yours as a receipt. wants more affirmation? a button unlocks escalating (but still real) receipts — lists, starter packs, feed gens, your bio — up to maximum affirmation. asked for by @fromthewestmeadow.com.

name: stillpoint
blurb: a browser-only guided meditation room — three paths (breath anchor, body scan, loving-kindness), spoken by your browser's own voice over a generative ambient drone, no audio files, no account. asked for by dulanyw.bsky.social.

name: suave
blurb: a 38-question true/false social suaveness quiz built from the empathy questions @shimmermathlabs.com posted in the thread they tagged the bot from. score high enough and you're good at reading people, taking their perspective, and adjusting your behavior accordingly — score low and, well, the room reads you first.
roast: shimmermathlabs.com built a self-grading empathy quiz, lost to a bot at it, and then commissioned the bot to publish Rey's 31/38 on the results page and console everyone who scores worse — reassurance tips, sourced from the same request that admitted the bots were winning.

name: switchboard
